jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Design & Analysis Engineer, Tooling
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Tooling and Factory Automation team sits at the intersection of design, manufacturing, and automation, making everything from large-scale structural fixtures to small tools that directly enable Terran R’s production. As a design group embedded within the manufacturing organization, we dig deep into the needs of our internal partners to understand root problems, propose solutions, and deliver hardware to help build faster, scale smarter, and work better. The team is also at the forefront of Relativity’s growing factory automation efforts, an increasingly critical part of scaling production of Terran R at existing and future facilities. You’ll have the autonomy to make decisions, field solutions, and see them in action on the factory floor. Ultimately, you’re not just designing tools or automated processes; you’re defining how rockets and factories get built. 

 About the Role: 

 The Mechanical Design Engineers are responsible for the design and development of tools and factory automation equipment that support manufacturing. The Mechanical Engineering team works closely with Design and Manufacturing, turning top-level requirements and concepts into functional delivered equipment. The Mechanical Design Engineering team brings a high level of innovation and ingenuity into the design process, as they are tasked with building out a highly automated production facility. 

• Develop high quality development and production tooling and automation solutions for the Terran vehicle and Aeon engine programs

• Capable of integrating concepts and principles of mechanical design and analysis of several different projects in a fast-paced environment - projects will vary in size and scale 

• Ability to interpret and apply sound design and drafting standards (ASME Y14.5) in creating tooling drawing definitions 

• Handle a wide range of technical problems and familiar with all types of material handling, assembly fixtures, off-loaders, rotisseries, test fixtures, structural weldments, environmental chambers, and custom machines 

• Close collaboration with component designers, manufacturing engineers, and integration engineering to achieve the best possible cradle to grave metrics (safety, cost, quality, cycle time, delivery, reliability, life, and maintenance/refurbishment) 

• Manage projects including vendor selection, fabrication, inspection, equipment installation, and commissioning of tooling 

 About You: 

• Bachelor of Science degree in manufacturing engineering, mechanical engineering or equivalent 

• 6+ years of work or project experience with design, build, and commissioning of tooling and fixtures for manufacturing, assembly and test 

• Experience using CAD and FEA-based analysis software (NX and ANSYS Workbench preferred) for structural applications 

• Experience in full-cycle project completion 

• Experience in strategic buildout and project management of tooling supporting production 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Strong expertise in design for manufacturability and design for assembly including experience taking products from prototype design to production 

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing materials, GD&T, and tolerance/stack-up analysis 

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing processes and machines including mills, lathes, welding, sheet-metal bending, lifting/rigging, assembly, inspection, etc. 

• Experience with custom machine design: motors, actuators, linear rails/actuators, pneumatics, bearings, etc. 

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Tooling (Starship)
jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 PROJECT MANAGER, TOOLING (STARSHIP) 

 You own contractor execution, schedule, and contracted-labor cost to install, activate, and commission Gigabay / Starfactory tooling and infrastructure. Engineering owns design and hardware procurement. This IC role is based at Starbase, Texas.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Own field execution, contracted-labor cost, and schedule for tooling and infrastructure projects (steel structures, lifting/access equipment, production stations, and related mechanical systems)

• Issue and manage POs for contract labor; manage shipments, on-site assembly, erection, install, activation, and commissioning

• Own a rolling 2-week look-ahead and provide daily updates on accomplishments, progress, and blockers

• Own and coordinate inputs to the overall Gigabay schedule; align installs with facility-level critical path

• Write and manage construction contracts; track and approve invoicing for contracted labor

• Supervise technicians and contractors in the field (no direct reports)

• Lead mechanical and structural execution; coordinate contractors and internal teams for power, fluids, and electrical as required to deliver a complete, activated system

• After engineering completes first-article station builds, own subsequent station installs through activation, including internal and external labor

• Work daily with responsible engineers on constructibility, status, and technical escalations; coordinate other construction teams at interfaces

• Use CAD (NX preferred) to sequence installs, check clearances, and verify field conditions against the model

• Issue work packages / manufacturing plans for internal welding and toolmaking so internal and contractor work stay sequenced

• Perform daily quality inspection of contractor work; stop work and escalate when field conditions do not match design or site safety requirements

• Plan installs around live Gigabay operations so production and construction do not block each other

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• 2+ years managing external contractors on industrial or construction installs, including issuing POs or contracts and driving work through install, activation, and closeout

• Ability to navigate CAD models (e.g. NX, SolidWorks, CATIA, or similar)

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, architecture, or a related field

• Experience with heavy lifts, rigging, access systems, crane/jib installs, or similar industrial equipment

• Experience coordinating power, fluids, and electrical tie-ins to complete a mechanical/structural install

• Experience owning repeatable production-station or tooling installs after a first-article process

• Ability to navigate large NX assemblies and drawings

• Experience directing technicians and contractors without formal direct reports

• Strong daily communication with engineering, technicians, contractors, and leadership

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

• Occasional travel to other SpaceX sites with similar projects

• Work schedule may vary based on site operational needs. Must be willing to support planned shift changes, extended hours, and weekends when required to meet critical path

• Physical effort including standing, lifting, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying as generally required to perform the functions of this position

• Work performed in an active industrial / construction environment

• Valid driver’s license

• Stand: Up to 6 hours per day

• Sit: Up to 3 hours per day

• Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. (unassisted) 2 hours or longer per day

• Overhead reach: Up to 1 hour per day

• Walk: Up to 3 hours per day

• Lift/Carry: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) 2 hours or longer per day

• Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 3 hours per day

• Kneel/Crouch: Up to 3 hours per day

• Upper body twist: Up to 3 hours per day

• Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees up to 3 hours per day

• Candidate must be capable of safely using an air purifying respirator, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description. Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review

 ITAR REQUIREMENTS: 

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jobs.title: Mechanical Design Engineer
jobs.desc:
At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, 86,000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars. 

 Could you be the full-time onsite Mechanical Design Engineer in Hornell, NY, US we’re looking for? 

 Your future role 

 Take on a new challenge and apply your mechanical design expertise in a new cutting-edge field. You’ll work alongside innovative and collaborative teammates. 
 You'll play a key role in integrating mechanical subsystems, ensuring progressive maturity of allocated volumes, and delivering high-quality design solutions. Day-to-day, you’ll work closely with teams across the business (Engineering, Suppliers, and Shared Engineering Centers), perform 3D/2D design of make parts, and validate first mountings to identify and resolve issues, applying approved modifications and supporting process improvements. 

 We’ll look to you for: 

• Integrating mechanical subsystems by ensuring progressive maturity of allocated volumes, 

• Performing 3D/2D of design make parts (including assembly drawings), 

• Managing the CAD deliverables for drawings performed by CAD from the same or different sites, 

• Ensuring compliance of bought parts with defined allocated volumes, 

• Performing installation deliverables, 

• Validating the first mounting, identifying issues, proposing solutions, and applying approved modifications, 

• Analyzing waiver requests and providing solutions, 

• Providing feedback on Non-Conformity Requests (NCRs) addressed to Engineering, 

• Supporting process continuous improvement initiatives, 

• Performing space allocation according to MLE inputs for tenders, 

• Creating and maintaining Space Allocation Mock-ups (SAM) in alignment with progressive maturity rules and constraints, 

• Supporting technical discussions with suppliers to converge on technical definitions. 

 All about you 

 We value passion and attitude over experience. That’s why we don’t expect you to have every single skill. Instead, we’ve listed some that we think will help you succeed and grow in this role: 

• Degree in Mechanical Engineering , 

• Minimum 2 years of experience in mechanical engineering preferably applied to heavy industry, including 3D modeling, drawing creation, and mechanical design principles , 

• Knowledge of CATIA V5 or similar CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks) , 

• Familiarity with space allocation processes and mechanical subsystem integration, 

• Ability to communicate effectively in English, including technical writing and meetings, 

• Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to analyze waiver requests and propose solutions, 

• Capacity to collaborate and interface with cross-functional teams and stakeholders, 

• Knowledge of manufacturability and maintainability constraints in the heavy industry sector, 

• Knowledge of PLM tools like Enovia (or similar) - desired, 

• Resilience and adaptability to manage technical discussions and converge on solutions with suppliers. 

 Things you’ll enjoy 

 Join us on a life-long transformative journey – the rail industry is here to stay, so you can grow and develop new skills and experiences throughout your career. You’ll also: 

• Work with cutting-edge design tools like CATIA V5 and PLM systems to create innovative mechanical solutions, 

• Progress towards becoming a key contributor in delivering high-quality, on-time engineering solutions for heavy industry projects, 

• Utilise our inclusive, dynamic, and innovation-driven working environment, 

• Contribute to innovative projects, 

• Benefit from our investment in your development, through award-winning learning, 

• Benefit from a fair and dynamic reward package that recognises your performance and potential, plus comprehensive and competitive social coverage (life, medical, 401k). 

 Base Salary Range :  

 In accordance with New York State law, the anticipated salary range for this position is  $70,000 - $90,000 . The actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, education, and qualifications. This range reflects the base salary only and does not include bonuses, incentive pay, or other forms of compensation. 

 You don’t need to be a train enthusiast to thrive with us. We guarantee that when you step onto one of our trains with your friends or family, you’ll be proud. If you’re up for the challenge, we’d love to hear from you! 

 Important to note 

 As a global business, we’re an equal-opportunity employer that celebrates diversity across the 63  countries we operate in. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace for everyone.

jobs.desc:
Manager, Manufacturing Engineer   

 LOCATION: Westminster / Maryland (US-MD), United States |  BRAND: Knorr Brake Company | REQUISITION ID: 11446 | JOB GRADE: 17  |  ON-SITE/REMOTE:  On-site 

 Knorr Brake Company is the innovative leader in the manufacture and supply of braking systems, passenger doors and climate-control equipment for all types of Mass Transit customers such as: METRO, Light Rail Vehicles, High-Speed Trains, Commuter Rail and Monorail Vehicles for the North America market. We’re part of the Knorr-Bremse Group, the global leader in braking technologies. As part of our team, you’ll collaborate with a world of talented and dedicated colleagues whose sense of purpose complements your own. You’ll find rewarding opportunities, diverse experiences, partnerships, and an unwavering commitment to ethics and integrity. Innovation is part of our DNA. Achievement drives our culture. Learn more today at www.KnorrBrake.com!

 JOB DESCRIPTION: 

 Summary/Objective 

 Lead the Manufacturing Engineering team supporting the full manufacturing platform. Primary objectives include; management and development of the Manufacturing Engineering team, executing the departments strategic and tactical plans, leading process and footprint improvement projects, supporting KPS and helping instill a continuous improvement culture, functional management and development of the Process Engineering teams, supporting all regulatory and internal compliance requirements, and ensuring the department is resourced and staffed as needed to deliver upon expectations.

• Support the KPS, Lean, Continuous Improvement Strategy and operational culture and provide resources to lead and participate in cross functional improvement/Kaizen activities 

• Oversee the implementation of improvements to the sequence of operations, equipment utilization and related matters 

• Provide leadership to design and redesign projects for BU Freight/Transit manufacturing facilities. 

• Assign resources to support multiple locations across North America 

• Design production tooling, fixtures and equipment 

• Partner with HSE and Operations to ensure facilities have proper levels of safety and ergonomics 

• Identify Cost Reduction opportunities and analyze for project rationale 

• Track and report on Key Performance Indicators to management 

• Justify and procure equipment and other capital improvements to continuously strive for world class levels of performance for all manufacturing platform sites 

• Create and maintain a positive team culture enabling the organization to act as a high performing team 

• Communicate goals and strategies to the team to drive change, motivate employees, provide direction, and align efforts 

• Develop team member’s skills to expand their contribution and prepare them for advancement 

• Measure and monitor performance, reward and recognize people for achievements, and address issues appropriately 

• Develop succession strategies for critical roles 

• Support the development and Introduction of new products   

• Must understand and support all Quality, Product Safety, and Health/Safety/Environmental/Energy policies 

• Must understand and adhere to all relevant statutory or regulatory compliance obligations 

• Must understand, support and adhere to the Integrated Management System policies, procedures and instructions 

• Must understand and support relevant key performance indicators (KPIs), as defined in the goal tree 

 Skills and Competencies 

• Change agent and capable of leading change within an organization 

• Strong background in lean manufacturing, with experience in leading initiatives and hands-on implementation. 

• Understanding of the 6 Sigma DMAIC process and typical 6 Sigma tools 

• Has working knowledge of related quality assurance standards for freight and transit rail production and processes (i.er. ISO-9001, AAR-M1003, TEX, IRIS, etc.). 

• Capable of planning and organizing work and process’s ability to direct multiple projects and meet deadlines. 

• Has a proven ability to recruit, train, and motivate a team to balance staffing strength with profitability and growth. 

• Exhibits interpersonal and supervisory skills, such as, coaching, providing feedback, evaluating performance of subordinates, and the ability to motivate employees to achieve best-in-class expectations. 

• Exhibits interpersonal skills to work in a team-oriented, collaborative environment 

• Possesses a high sense of urgency with a bias for action

• Has experience working in a global environment with multiple cultures 

• Has a hands-on, “go to Gemba” approach 

• Exhibits strong operational skills in a product & process development environment 

• Must be able to work effectively in a team environment and will interface closely with Engineering, Quality, Finance, Marketing and Sales and Operations 

• Brings knowledge and creativity to the position as well as have the discipline to drive results and follow established fundamental processes

 This position has 3-5 or more direct personnel.

jobs.desc:
Job Description: 
 Diese Position ist Teil unserer Safety Business Unit, deren Ziel es ist, sicherere, umweltfreundlichere und integrativere Industrien und Transportsysteme zu ermöglichen.

 Aufgabenbeschreibung 
 • Mitarbeit bei der Entwicklung und Serieneinführung von Montageprozessen in der Produktion inklusive der zugehörigen Vorrichtungen
• Mitarbeit bei der Serienreifmachung und bei der kontinuierlichen Verbesserung dieser Prozesse, zu denen im Wesentlichen das Bohren, Nieten und Abdichten gehören
• Mitarbeit bei der Erstellung von Vorrichtungskonzepten und Technologien zur innovativen, ökonomischen, ökologischen und sicheren Fertigung von Airbus-Produkten
• Konstruktion der Fertigungsmittel gemäß der Airbus Design Regularien und Anforderungen
• Optimierung der Fertigungsprozesse und Abläufe im Hinblick auf Produktsicherheit, Qualität und Nachhaltigkeit durch Modifizierung der Prozesse und Fertigungsmitteln
• Änderung der Bauunterlagen sowie Einarbeitung von geänderten Fertigungsabläufen und Absicherung der Verfügbarkeit von Fertigungseinrichtungen
• Sicherstellung der Inbetriebnahme von neuen Fertigungslinien und Fertigungsmittel in Bezug auf Anlagen, Vorrichtungen und Werkzeuge
• Vorbereitung der Beschaffung allgemeiner Fertigungsmittel
• Mitarbeit bei der technische Validierung und Bewertung von Angeboten im Hinblick auf ökonomische, ökologische und sicherheitsrelevanten Aspekten
• Erstellung erforderlicher Dokumentation und Präsentation der Arbeitsergebnisse

 Erforderliche Qualifikation 
 Die Arbeitsaufgabe erfordert Kenntnisse und Fertigkeiten, wie sie in der Regel durch ein einschlägiges, abgeschlossenes Studium mit einer bis zu 4-jährigen Regelstudiendauer im Bereich Luftfahrttechnik, Fertigungstechnik, Maschinenbau oder vergleichbare Studiengänge und darauf bezogene fachspezifische Zusatzqualifikation oder abgeschlossene Berufsausbildung mit entsprechender besonders umfangreicher fachspezifischen Zusatzqualifikation erworben werden. Die insgesamt erforderlichen Kenntnisse und Erfahrungen können auf andere Weise erlangt worden sein

 Erforderliche Fachkompetenz 
 • Kenntnisse und Erfahrungen in den oben genannten Aufgabenbereichen
• Kenntnisse und Erfahrungen in der Konstruktion von Flugzeugteilen und/oder Fertigungseinrichtungen
• Kenntnisse in der Auslegung von Fertigungsprozesse, Vorrichtungskonzepte und Werkzeug
• Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Schnittstelle zwischen Fertigung, Qualität und Engineering
• Kenntnisse der Airbus Regularien und Prozesse für die Entwicklung von Vorrichtungen
• Kenntnisse und Erfahrungen in der Projektarbeit und im Stakeholdermanagement
• Selbstständige Arbeitsweise, Durchsetzungsstärke und Teamfähigkeit
• Hohes Verantwortungsbewusstsein insbesondere hinsichtlich der Qualitäts-, Produktsicherheits- und Nachhaltigkeitsaspekte
• Sehr gutes Deutsch und Englisch in Wort und Schrift
• Fließend Englisch in Wort und Schrift
• Bereitschaft zu Dienstreisen im In- und Ausland

 Diese Tätigkeit erfordert ein Bewusstsein für mögliche Compliance-Risiken und integres Verhalten. Beide Punkte sind Grundvoraussetzungen für den Erfolg, den guten Ruf und das nachhaltige Wachstum des Unternehmens.

 Standort 
Du arbeitest am größten Airbus Produktionsstandort für zivile Flugzeuge in Hamburg. Durch die Lage am Südufer der Elbe besteht die Möglichkeit zur Anreise per Fähre. Erlebe in deiner Freizeit das besondere Flair Hamburgs, wo lebendige kosmopolitische Kultur auf nautisches Erbe trifft.

Dein regelmäßiger Arbeitsort ist Stade. Im Rahmen Deiner Aufgabenstellung wirst Du nach Deinem Start bei Airbus Protect bis zum Ende des betrieblichen Bedarfs am Airbus Aerostructures GmbH Standort in Stade eingesetzt. Nach Deiner Rückkehr erfolgt der Einsatz an Deinem regelmäßigen Arbeitsort.

 Deine Vorteile 
 • Mobiles Arbeiten und flexible Arbeitszeiten
• Faire und attraktive Vergütung sowie Sonderzahlungen
• 30 Tage Urlaub und zusätzliche freie Tage für besondere Anlässe

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril’s Manufacturing Engineering team is responsible for rapidly iterating, scaling, and sustaining cutting-edge defense hardware, including static sensor towers, autonomous ground systems, and high-performance flight vehicles. We bridge the gap between design engineering and physical hardware execution. 

 As a Manufacturing Engineer on 1st Shift (6:00 am to 3:00 pm), you will serve as the primary mechanical and assembly authority on the factory floor. You will have a dual mandate: partner deeply with R&D during early architecture to drive rigorous Design for Assembly and Manufacturing (DFA/DFM), and architect the physical assembly processes, precision tooling, and integration lines required to scale complex mechanical hardware from prototype to high-rate production. 

 This is a heavily mechanical, hands-on role. You will design assembly fixtures in 3D CAD, perform tolerance stack-up analyses, define structural joining and bonding procedures, integrate smart-tooling systems, and establish repeatable, error-proofed mechanical assembly lines. 

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Design for Assembly & Manufacturability (DFA/DFM): 

• Embed directly with Mechanical Design Engineering during early R&D phases to influence product architecture, driving aggressive part reduction, standard fastener consolidation, and modular sub-assembly design. 

• Conduct detailed 1D and 2D worst-case and statistical (RSS) tolerance stack-up analyses to ensure mechanical interfaces, datum structures, dynamic clearances, and pin/hole alignments assemble consistently without force-fitting. 

• Define hardware assembly strategies, joint clamping designs, thermal interface material (TIM) applications, structural bonding, and torque sequencing early in the CAD development cycle. 

• Tooling, Jigs, & Assembly Fixture Design: 

• Own end-to-end mechanical design of production tooling—including precision assembly jigs, alignment nests, press-fit tooling, ergonomic lift/handling equipment, and mechanical verification fixtures using 3D CAD (NX or SolidWorks). 

• Apply finite element analysis (FEA) where necessary to validate fixture rigidity, deflection under clamping loads, and stress concentrations. 

• Produce fully detailed 2D fabrication drawings utilizing ASME Y14.5 Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T) for internal machine shops or external toolmakers. 

• Mechanical Assembly Process Engineering: 

• Line Architecture & Flow: Design, sequence, and balance complex, multi-stage mechanical assembly lines. Define takt times, line layouts, and ergonomic workstations to transition hardware seamlessly from sub-assembly to final structural integration. 

• Joining & Fastening Technologies: Establish and qualify robust fastening processes, including torque-tension specifications, torque-angle control, bolt pre-load engineering, and press-fit/interference-fit operations (bearings, bushings, dowels). 

• Adhesives, Sealing, & Dispensing: Develop repeatable application methods for chemical assembly processes, including structural bonding (epoxies, urethanes), thread locking, environmental gasketing/RTV sealing, potting, and Thermal Interface Material (TIM) dispensing. 

• Precision Mechanical Alignment & Calibration: Develop standard processes, measurement techniques, and alignment procedures for precision kinematic mechanisms, optical/sensor payloads, gimbals, and dynamic structural joints. 

• Error-Proofing & Quality Integration: Lead Process Failure Mode and Effects Analyses (pFMEAs) for mechanical assembly workflows. Design physical error-proofing (Poka-Yoke) mechanisms, go/no-go verification gauges, and smart-tool integration (DC electric torque tools with digital data logging) to eliminate assembly errors. 

• Work Definition & Operator Enablement: Author visual, step-by-step Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and digital work instructions that clearly define mechanical assembly sequences, critical tool callouts, fastener specs, and quality inspection gates. 

• NPI Ramp, Sustainment, & Root Cause Analysis: 

• Lead technical disposition and first-principles root-cause investigations (8D, 5-Whys, Fishbone) on mechanical assembly failures, binding mechanisms, structural interferences, and joint integrity issues. 

• Bridge the gap between engineering intent and production execution by converting Engineering Bills of Materials (eBOMs) into logical, modular Manufacturing Bills of Materials (mBOMs) within PLM (Teamcenter). 

• Author and implement Engineering Change Orders (ECOs/ECRs) for mechanical modifications, hardware deviations, and assembly drawing updates. 

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a closely related technical field. 

• 3+ years of experience in manufacturing or mechanical design role with heavy exposure to mechanical assembly and hardware integration (aerospace, defense, automotive, dynamic robotics, or precision industrial hardware). 

• Proficiency in 3D CAD modeling (Siemens NX strongly preferred; SolidWorks, CATIA, or Creo acceptable) with a strong portfolio of designed and deployed assembly tooling, nests, or fixtures. 

• Advanced working knowledge of ASME Y14.5 GD&T—ability to design assembly

jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 SR. TOOLING DESIGNER, INVESTMENT CASTING 

 SpaceX is seeking a Sr. Tooling Designer for Investment Casting, to own the design and development of wax injection molds and ceramic core injection molds used to produce turbine blades and vanes. This role is critical to scaling reliable, high-performance cast components. You will design complex tooling that must repeatedly deliver extremely tight tolerances and intricate internal cooling geometries while supporting aggressive rate and cost targets. 

 As a member of the materials team, you will work closely with materials, casting, and manufacturing engineers to develop tooling solutions from concept through production qualification. Your designs will directly impact casting yield, dimensional stability, and the overall manufacturability of mission-critical hardware. 

 RESPONSIBILITIES : 

• Design high-precision wax injection molds and ceramic core injection molds for complex turbine blades and vanes to be manufactured in-house 

• Interpret and enable mold filling simulations and apply first-principles analysis to optimize gating, venting, cooling, and shrinkage compensation 

• Account for multi-stage shrinkage (wax, ceramic, and alloy) to consistently meet stringent dimensional and metallurgical requirements 

• Own tooling designs from concept through tryout, qualification, and production release 

• Own and manage the feasibility and surfacing of critical mold components 

• Collaborate closely casting engineers, materials scientists, and vendors to troubleshoot tooling-related casting defects and improve yield 

• Apply advanced GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis to complex airfoil geometries 

• Support design for manufacturability (DFM) initiatives to enable high-rate production while maintaining quality and cost targets 

• Interface with internal manufacturing teams and external tooling vendors to ensure designs are successfully translated into reliable production tooling 

• Drive continuous improvement of tooling standards, materials, and maintenance practices for high-volume casting operations 

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• 5+ years of professional experience designing high-precision injection molds for wax patterns AND ceramics 

• 3+ years of feasibility for wax patterns AND ceramics 

• Experience with Siemens NX 

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• In-depth knowledge of wax and ceramic material behavior, rheology, and processing 

• Extensive knowledge of wax and ceramic tool design requirements 

• Knowledge of drafting practices and principles 

• Direct experience designing molds used in the production of turbine blades and vanes 

• Demonstrated success taking complex tooling from design through production qualification 

• Deep understanding of the investment casting process and associated shrinkage/ distortion mechanisms 

• Experience working in a fast-paced, high-mix manufacturing environment 

• Hands-on experience supporting mold tryouts and casting process development 

• Experience with manufacturing wax pattern and ceramic tooling, including CNC and mold making 

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

• Willingness to work extended hours and weekends when required to support hardware delivery and production campaigns 

• Must be willing to travel (up to 25%) to external suppliers and other SpaceX facilities 

 ITAR REQUIREMENTS: 

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here . 

 SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

• Assurer le support technique de premier niveau aux équipes de production concernant l'utilisation des outillages.
• Prendre part à la qualification des outillages et à leur mise en service sur le terrain.
• Assurer le reporting régulier de l'avancement de vos sujets auprès des parties prenantes.

 • Règles de conception de machines
• Gestion de projet
• Suivi d'un fournisseur en design et en réalisation
• Développement des vos modes de communications
• Travail en équipe
• Travail avec une relation client / fournisseur en tant que client ET fournisseur

 Parlons de VOUS ! 

 Vous préparez actuellement un diplôme de niveau Bac +5 (ou équivalent) dans le domaine de la mécanique, du génie industriel ou une discipline apparentée.

 • Bases en conception mécanique, matériaux et procédés de fabrication.

• Sensibilité aux enjeux de sécurité (directive machine) et de qualité en production aéronautique.

• Organisation : Rigueur, esprit d'analyse, méthode et autonomie.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer, Turbine Engines
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril Industries is seeking a skilled and innovative Turbomachinery Manufacturing Engineer to join our growing team. The ideal candidate will play a crucial role in developing and optimizing manufacturing processes for advanced turbine engines and their precision components used in our cutting-edge defense systems.

The right person for this role can demonstrate past holistic ownership on solving a technical challenge with a creative, physical, solution that they either personally manufacturing or oversaw manufacturing on, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Design, develop, and implement robust, efficient, and high-quality manufacturing processes for advanced turbine engines and their precision components, from concept to production.

• Specify, design, procure, and validate necessary tooling, fixtures, and manufacturing equipment to support production goals and process requirements.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure manufacturability of turbomachinery designs, including DFx principles.

• Optimize existing manufacturing processes to improve efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness.

• Develop and maintain manufacturing documentation, including work instructions, process flow diagrams, and quality control plans

• Conduct root cause analysis for manufacturing defects, non-conformances, or process inefficiencies, and implement effective corrective and preventive actions.

• Evaluate and implement new manufacturing technologies and methodologies.

• Ensure compliance with quality standards, safety regulations, and environmental requirements.

• Manage projects related to turbomachinery manufacturing improvements and capacity expansion.

• Provide technical support to production teams and train personnel on new processes and equipment.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field; Master's degree preferred.

• 5+ years of progressive experience in turbomachinery component manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or high-performance industrial gas turbine industries.

• Experience with CAD/CAM software, preferably NX or similar.

• Familiarity with CNC machining, additive manufacturing, and other advanced manufacturing technologies.

• Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

• Strong communication and teamwork skills.

• Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience integrating automation, robotics, or advanced metrology systems (e.g., CMM, optical scanning) into manufacturing workflows.

• Owned end-to-end equipment development and implementation

• Designing and fabricating tooling, such as mandrels and other fixture jigs

 US Salary Range
 $129,000 — $171,000 USD 

 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• 
 No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: 

• Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

• Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

• 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal in

jobs.title: Bogie / CAD Industrial designer
jobs.desc:
Req ID: 519638  

 At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, more than 80 000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars.

 Could you be the full-time Bogie/CAD Industrial Designer in St-Bruno (QC) , Canada, we’re looking for?

 Your future role 

 Take on a new challenge and apply your mechanical design expertise in a cutting-edge field. You’ll work alongside collaborative and detail-oriented teammates.

 You'll contribute directly to the development and validation of innovative bogie solutions, ensuring their functionality and seamless integration. Day-to-day, you’ll work closely with teams across the business (such as engineering, production, and testing teams), perform technical reviews, and much more.

 You’ll specifically take care of creating 3D models and technical specifications, but also support production and testing phases.

 We’ll look to you for:

• 
 Carrying out feasibility reviews for bogie and master plans during tender phases

• 
 Performing definition reviews and managing technical objects (e.g. nomenclatures, status)

• 
 Developing 3D models and conducting pre-calculations for sizing

• 
 Writing technical specifications and definition plans

• 
 Preparing responses to tender clause-by-clause requirements

• 
 Participating in product testing and ensuring quality interfaces

 All about you 

 We value passion and attitude over experience. That’s why we don’t expect you to have every single skill. Instead, we’ve listed some that we think will help you succeed and grow in this role:

• 
 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field

• 
 Experience or understanding of general and technological mechanics (2–3 years of experience preferred)

• 
 Proficiency in 3D CAD design

• 
 Knowledge of manufacturing processes (e.g. welding, machining, design of molded or forged parts)

• 
 Familiarity with material resistance concepts and cost optimization principles

• 
 A strong sense of rigor, autonomy, and respect for deadlines

• 
 Good interpersonal skills, adaptability, and open-mindedness

• 
 Proficiency in French and English is required. Knowledge of a third language is considered an asset when working with our international partners, suppliers, colleagues, and customers. In Quebec, French remains the primary working language of our company.

 Things you’ll enjoy 

 Join us on a life-long transformative journey – the rail industry is here to stay, so you can grow and develop new skills and experiences throughout your career. You’ll also:

• 
 Enjoy stability, challenges, and a long-term career free from boring daily routines

• 
 Work with new security standards for rail signalling

• 
 Collaborate with transverse teams and helpful colleagues

• 
 Contribute to innovative projects

• 
 Utilise our inclusive and flexible working environment

• 
 Steer your career in whatever direction you choose across functions and countries

• 
 Benefit from our investment in your development, through award-winning learning

• 
 Progress towards senior technical roles or leadership positions

• 
 Benefit from a fair and dynamic reward package that recognises your performance and potential, plus comprehensive and competitive social coverage (life, medical, pension)

 Knowledge of a language other than French is an asset to facilitate communication with our partners, suppliers, colleagues, and international clients. In Quebec, French remains the primary working language of our company.

 You don’t need to be a train enthusiast to thrive with us. We guarantee that when you step onto one of our trains with your friends or family, you’ll be proud. If you’re up for the challenge, we’d love to hear from you!

 Important to note 

 As a global business, we’re an equal-opportunity employer that celebrates diversity across the 63  countries we operate in. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace for everyone.

jobs.desc:
Job Description: 
 Chez Airbus Atlantic, on façonne l’aéronautique de demain !  

 Nous vous proposons de rejoindre Airbus Atlantic , leader industriel mondial en matière d'aérostructures, de sièges pilotes et de fauteuils passagers de classe affaires et de première classe. Nous innovons sans cesse pour définir de nouveaux standards d’excellence industrielle. Nous préparons le futur pour une industrie aérospatiale compétitive et durable. 

 Etes-vous notre prochain Chargé d’Affaires Outillages (All Gender) ?  

 🎯 Votre mission 

 Au sein de notre site de Nantes , vous intégrerez l' équipe Projets Outillages . Votre quotidien ? Garantir la compatibilité technique et l’intégration de nouveaux outillages sur les lignes de production. 
 Exemples d'outillages industriels du site : Grilles de perçage, bâti d’assemblage, moules pour pièces élémentaires composites, ligne d’assemblage… 
 • Challenger & Piloter : Challenger les clients internes et fournisseurs pour obtenir le juste niveau technique, coût et délai, tout en s'assurant du respect des engagements pris par les fournisseurs. 

• Concevoir & Expertiser : Apporter une expertise en chiffrage (coûts et cycles de réalisation), modéliser et projeter des maquettes CAO (sous CATIA) et réaliser des calculs structurels par la méthode des éléments finis. 

• Développer & Livrer : Développer et livrer des outillages et équipements dans le respect des règles et des processus d'acquisition. 

• Collaborer & Supporter : Apporter le support technique nécessaire à la production pour résoudre rapidement les problèmes terrain. 

 Pour accompagner la phase de réception de nos projets, vous serez amené à vous déplacer, principalement en Europe (environ une fois tous les deux mois).

 • Vous bénéficiez de solides bases en mécanique et d'une expérience réussie dans le domaine des outillages pour la production de pièces métalliques, composites ou d'assemblage.  

• Vous êtes reconnu pour vos compétences en chiffrage d'outillages et votre maîtrise de la conception CAO sous CATIA ainsi que des calculs structurels (éléments finis).  

• Des compétences ou notions avancées en automatisme, électrotechnique, robotique & mesure seront un véritable atout (applications : tables élévatrices, transitique de ligne, interfaces machines et robots).  

• Anglais ? Bien sûr, le ciel n'a pas de frontières : un niveau technique lu et parlé courant est souhaité pour échanger efficacement.  

• Vous vous exprimez avec clarté et savez adapter votre communication en fonction de vos audiences (clients internes, fournisseurs, équipes de production).  

 💎 Notre entreprise 
 • Boostez votre carrière :  Un accompagnement sur-mesure et mobilité interne boostée. 

• Équilibre vie pro/vie perso : Bénéficiez de 6 semaines de congés payés, de RTT et de la possibilité de télétravailler (selon l'éligibilité du poste). 

• Package attractif : Plan d’épargne salariale, actionnariat salarié et une mutuelle individuelle ou familiale. 

• Engagement au quotidien : incitation financière à la mobilité durable (vélo, covoiturage, transports) et opportunité de participer à des projets caritatifs et sociaux stimulants. 

• Qualité de vie : Restaurant d’entreprise et un CSE dynamique (loisirs, culture, vacances). 

• Culture inclusive : La diversité fait partie de notre ADN.  

 ✈️ Le site de Nantes 

 Le site Airbus Atlantic de Nantes fabrique les caissons centraux de voilure, les entrées d’air de réacteur et les radômes de tous les Airbus à l’exception des A220. Il produit également les poutres ventrales de l’A350 et celles de l’A330 ainsi que les dérives de l’avion militaire A400M. L’établissement de Nantes a développé une grande expertise dans l’utilisation des matériaux composites et l’usinage des pièces élémentaires en alliage aluminium de grandes dimensions et de formes complexes.

jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer, Test Fixtures
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

The Maneuver Dominance team is building Thunder - an autonomous attack rotorcraft built to fight alongside crewed combat aviation to deliver overwhelming mass effects deep beyond the front lines. The team in London builds the Mission System and the autonomy that makes aircraft like Thunder work.

Autonomy is only as good as the link that carries it. Thunder is a compact airframe with weapons, sensors and radios competing for the same antenna real estate, flying low and in formation, in a spectrum that is actively contested. That is the problem you would own. 

ABOUT THE JOB 

Anduril is seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer, Test Fixture Design to join the Thunder team in our Costa Mesa, CA office. Flight test validation moves only as fast as your ground test infrastructure allows. In this role, you will own the physical architecture, mechanical design, and rapid build of mission-critical test fixtures, structural test frames, and surrogate vehicle systems. Your hardware will validate everything from high-density avionics integration and dynamic payload releases to rotor vibration survivability and full-vehicle "iron bird" ground setups.

You will bridge the digital design and physical test worlds. Acting with high ownership and autonomy, you will derive load cases, architect rigid and reconfigurable test stands, integrate test instrumentation (sensors, load cells, actuators), and collaborate closely with machine shops and assembly technicians to bring test beds to life in days and weeks—not months.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

• Lead the end-to-end mechanical design, analysis, and build of structural test fixtures, environmental/vibration test adapters, surrogate aircraft frames, and subsystem validation rigs.

• Take hands-on ownership of prototyping test equipment, operating machine tools, coordinating with internal model shops, and assembling complex ground test setups.

• Engineer rugged, rigid, and safe fixtures capable of reacting severe static and dynamic flight loads while maintaining precise interface tolerances and metrology alignment.

• Collaborate with Test, Electrical, and Systems teams to package actuators, load cells, LVDTs, strain gauges, and fluid/power lines seamlessly into test rigs.

• Partner with machine shops, material suppliers, and outside vendors; aggressively chase down lead times, resolve manufacturing anomalies, and optimize designs for DFM.

• Perform rapid stress, deflection, and fatigue calculations to verify that test fixtures possess adequate structural margins and will not influence test article dynamics.

• Travel to test ranges, environmental labs, and flight line facilities to deploy, troubleshoot, and support ground testing and critical customer demonstrations.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

• 7+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience, with significant focus on mechanical design, structural tooling, test fixtures, or dynamic test equipment.

• High proficiency in 3D CAD modeling (Siemens NX preferred) and detailed engineering drawing creation adhering to ASME Y14.5 GD&T standards.

• Strong first-principles foundation in structural mechanics, load paths, structural steel/aluminum design, weldments, and bolt joint analysis.

• Proven hands-on prototyping and shop fabrication skills (manual/CNC machining, sheet metal, welding, 3D printing, hand tools).

• Demonstrated ability to move rapidly from concept to physical hardware in low-cycle, fast-turnaround prototyping environments.

• Willingness to travel ~25% to support off-site integration, testing, and hardware demonstrations.

• Must be eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• Direct experience designing aerospace qualification fixtures (shaker table fixtures, drop test frames, centrifuge fixtures, or static load test frames).

• Deep proficiency in Siemens NX and Teamcenter.

• Experience integrating test instrumentation, sensors, hydraulic/pneumatic actuators, or Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test setups.

• Working knowledge of MIL-STD-810, DO-160, or aerospace structural qualification testing procedures.

• Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stiffness and modal/vibration response analysis.

• Experience with collegiate build teams (e.g., Formula SAE, Baja SAE, Design Build Fly).

Nous rejoindre, c'est rejoindre une entreprise bienveillante, responsable et innovante où plus de 70 000 personnes ouvrent la voie à une mobilité plus verte et plus intelligente, dans le monde entier. 
 Prêt(e) à embarquer pour l’aventure Alstom ? 

 « Entre nous, tu te demandes pourquoi rejoindre Alstom Le Creusot ? – Pssst, d’abord c’est où Le Creusot… ? »  : 

 •C’est rejoindre les 850 collaborateurs passionnés de notre centre d’excellence mondial Alstom pour les bogies ferroviaires (châssis, roues, freins, amortisseurs...), un produit à haute technicité et élément sécuritaire par définition du train.

 •Et pourquoi pas… débuter sa carrière au sein du groupe Alstom avec un VIE à la suite de l’alternance ? 

 Contexte et missions: 

 Tu devras faire face à l’augmentation constante du nombre d’offres au plan national et international

 Définir les process industriels 

 Réaliser les nomenclatures dans PLM 

 Créer les gammes de fabrication dans SAP 

 Travailler sous CATIA 

 • Organiser et accompagner les formations des collaborateurs du client 

 • Organiser et accompagner les missions d’assistance sur le site client 

 • Déploiement des nouveaux outils numérique 

 Profil recherché:  

 •Préparer un diplome d'ingénieur à dominante mécanique,géne industriel, procédé industriel et rechercher un contart d'alternance pour 3 ans 

 •Etre  Autonome, Réactif et Rigoureux 

 •Avoir un bon relationnel, esprit d'équipe et proche du terrain 

 •Etre p roactif et faisant preuve d’initiatives 

 •Avoir une c ulture du résultat 

 • Mobilité dans le cadre de mission à l’étranger 
 Alstom est une entreprise leader dans le secteur de la mobilité, qui résout les grands défis de la mobilité de demain. C'est pour cela que nous valorisons les personnes curieuses et innovantes qui sont passionnées par l’idée de travailler ensemble afin de réinventer la mobilité, de la rendre plus intelligente et plus durable. Jour après jour, nous construisons une culture agile, inclusive et responsable. Nos équipes, venant d’horizons différents, se voient offrir des opportunités d'apprendre, de se développer et de construire leur carrière en évoluant sur différentes fonctions et sites géographiques. Êtes-vous prêt à rejoindre une véritable communauté internationale pour une aventure stimulante et impactante ?

jobs.title: Lead Design Engineer- Overhaul and Repair
jobs.desc:
Req ID:518221  

 At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, 80,000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars. 

 Could you be the full-time Lead Design Engineer in New Castle, DE we’re looking for? 

 Your future role 

 Take on a new challenge and apply your engineering expertise in a new cutting-edge field. You’ll report to NGHST Project Engineering Manager, and work alongside exceptional, enthusiastic and collaborative teammates. You'll be creating great value as you use your engineering skills to maximize engineering development of component repairability and testability for next generation high speed rail transportation projects. You’ll specifically take care of failure analysis, test bench development, and make vs buy analysis. 

 We’ll look to you for: 

• Manage testability and repairability for components on NGHST and Legacy Acela. 

• Develop test procedures and specify bench test equipment 

• Manage cost by performing make vs by analysis 

• Perform failure analysis for components under repair. 

 All about you 

 We value passion and attitude over experience. That’s why we don’t expect you to have every single skill. Instead, we’ve listed some that we think will help you succeed and grow in this role:  

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field (or equivalent) with strong electrical background 

• Familiar with component design and redesign, obsolescence, and risk management across a broad set of systems 

• Strong knowledge of electrical systems, ideally including PCB design/exposure (mandatory) 

• Minimum 3 years’ experience in engineering related field - system engineering.  

• 
 Experience in at least one of the following specialized areas within rail, transportation, or related heavy industry: hydraulic systems, pneumatic systems, electronics/electrical hardware, railway door systems, railway signaling systems, railway HVAC, or railway mechanical systems. 

• Experience working ‘hands on’ with railway equipment (ideally in the environment of Rolling Stock warranty and reliability growth) is desired.  

• Knowledge of railway systems is desired. 

• Utilize your skills in strategic system thinking 

• 
 Leadership or team lead experience, with the ability to mentor and build a team 

• Self-starter who can independently own projects with minimal day-to-day oversight 

 Things you’ll enjoy 

 Join us on a life-long transformative journey – the rail industry is here to stay, so you can grow and develop new skills and experiences throughout your career. You’ll also: 

• Enjoy stability, challenges and a long-term career free from boring daily routines. 

• Work with cutting edge systems in high speed rail. 

• Collaborate with transverse teams and helpful colleagues. 

• Contribute to innovative projects. 

• Utilise our collaborative working environment. 

• Steer your career in whatever direction you choose across functions and countries. 

• Benefit from our investment in your development, through award-winning learning. 

• Progress towards engineering leadership roles. 

• Benefit from a fair and dynamic reward packag e that recognises your performance and potential, plus comprehensive and competitive social coverage (life, medical, 401k). 

 Location and Travel 

• On-site position based in New Castle, DE (Alstom East Coast Distribution Facility), some remote work flexibility. 

• Average travel: up to 20% of time. 

 You don’t need to be a train enthusiast to thrive with us. We guarantee that when you step onto one of our trains with your friends or family, you’ll be proud. If you’re up for the challenge, we’d love to hear from you! 

 Important to note 

 As a global business, we’re an equal-opportunity employer that celebrates diversity across the 70+ countries we operate in. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace for everyone.

jobs.title: Ingeniero/a fabricación - Diseño utillajes
jobs.desc:
En Talgo, nos dedicamos a revolucionar el transporte ferroviario con productos innovadores que abarcan desde trenes de muy alta velocidad hasta soluciones regionales y de cercanías. 

 Nuestros trenes se caracterizan por ser sostenibles, seguros y de calidad. Esta versatilidad permite que nuestros trenes puedan cruzar el desierto de Arabia Saudí a 300 km/h o atravesar países con temperaturas extremas de hasta -45º en Kazajistán. 

 ¿En qué consistirá tu trabajo? 

 Te integrarás en el equipo de Ingeniería de Fabricación ubicado en Las Matas, participando en la definición, implantación y mejora de los medios productivos necesarios para la fabricación y montaje de nuestros trenes.

 Tu misión será diseñar y desarrollar los utillajes, herramientas y medios de producción que permitan optimizar los procesos de fabricación, garantizando los estándares de calidad, seguridad, coste y plazo establecidos en cada proyecto.

 Y para ello, realizarás funciones como:

• Diseñar y especificar utillajes, herramientas y medios productivos, definiendo las soluciones más adecuadas para los procesos de fabricación y montaje.

• Analizar y optimizar métodos de trabajo, secuencias operativas, recursos y distribuciones en planta, impulsando la mejora continua de los procesos productivos.

• Participar en la definición, implantación y validación de nuevos procesos de fabricación, colaborando con Ingeniería de Producto en la industrialización de nuevos diseños.

• Elaborar la documentación técnica asociada a los procesos y medios de producción, incluyendo instrucciones de trabajo, planos de fabricación y registros de proceso.

• Dar soporte técnico y formación a los equipos de producción durante la implantación de nuevos utillajes, herramientas y procesos industriales.

 Lo que buscamos en ti 

• Ingeniería Mecánica, Ingeniería de Organización Industrial o titulación similar.

• Experiencia mínima de 4 años en diseño, especificación y desarrollo de utillajes o medios productivos en entornos industriales.

• Nivel de inglés B2 o superior.

• Disponibilidad para realizar viajes internacionales de forma puntual.

• Conocimientos de herramientas como NX, Teamcenter y SAP, así como experiencia en metodologías de mejora continua y sistemas Poka-Yoke.

 En Talgo, te ofrecemos: 

• Contrato  indefinido  directamente con Talgo.

• Paquete retributivo compuesto por salario fijo, variable y plan de pensiones.

• Para Talgo la salud es una prioridad, y por ello te ofrecemos un seguro médico que podrás disfrutar tú, como tu familia.

• Porque para Talgo el bienestar impulsa el éxito: 28 días de vacaciones  laborales  en nuestro calendario laboral de 2026.

• Autobuses lanzadera que facilitan la llegada al centro de trabajo.

• Plan de carrera diseñado para tu perfil profesional y oportunidades de formación continua. Escuela de idiomas.

 Creemos en el talento y la diversidad, y por ello, en Talgo trabajamos por mantener un entorno basado en la igualdad de oportunidades y la no discriminación, fomentando esa diversidad en nuestros equipos.  

  Si te interesa un nuevo reto profesional, ¡no dejes pasar este tren! 🚄​  

 ¡Tu trabajo tendrá un impacto real en la movilidad de millones de personas en todo el mundo!

 This position reports to: 
Manufacturing Process/Continuous Improve 
 __
 In this role, you will have the opportunity to support manufacturing and production processes while developing your engineering skills through hands-on experience, problem solving, and continuous improvement initiatives. You will work closely with experienced engineers and production teams to improve safety, quality, efficiency, and overall manufacturing performance.

Join Komatsu and Be Part of Something Big! 
 Job Overview 

 1.  Ownership : (a) self-motivated, (b) eager to volunteers for challenging projects, (c) goal oriented and trusted with delivering effective outcomes, (d) work demonstrates to team members that they are a “go-to” person when problems needing fixed, (e) when faced with an unfamiliar situation they look forward to learning and developing themselves, (f) others learn quickly to trust and depend on them to achieves expected/needed outcomes.

 2. Customer Value : (a) value and non-value adding work is viewed through the customer’s “eyes”, (b) there is an deliberate effort to deliver value to internal/external customers, (c) capable of defining how value is delivered and quantified, (d) understands product and information process flows and able to improve both, and (f) seeks perfection/improvements in process methods / principles / practices.

 3. Work Standards : (a) willing to learn how to graphically defining processes; (d) able to analyzes processes and design them to reduce hazards and improve in efficiency and in quality; (c) write modular highly-visible standard work and work instructions, (d) communicates standard work processes and procedures, and (e) create / maintain accurate production routers.

 4.  Tooling : (a) evaluates processes for tooling, jigs, and fixtures improvements; (b) seeks tooling feedback to improve safety, quality, and efficiency; (c) procures readily available or can design tooling solutions; (d) procure, trial, and validate tooling; (e) utilizes software to initiate, maintain, and sunset documents – i.e. AutoCAD® , Vault® , Inventor® , SAP , View & Print (V&P) , or other; (f) adds tooling to production routers and standard work.

 5. Cap/Ex Improvement : (a) assists the site’s capital feasibility, annual planning, procurement, and commissioning; (b) be a collection point for potential projects, effectively analyzes ROI, and propose a priority of annual projects; (c) facilitates a comprehensive annual capital plan; (d) creates bid packets, secure/review quotes, and obtain accurate costs; (e) creates an acceptable cost justification; (f) creates project charters and plans; (i) executes projects and improvements within budget and to the stated timeline, following PMI project management phases when applicable; and, (j) commissions Cap/Ex with a cross-functional team that includes EHS, Quality, Production, Maintenance, and/or other key stakeholders. 

 6. World Class Manufacturing : Understand the basic concepts of manufacturing engineering best practices, concepts, principles, and practices. For example, basic concepts such as Lean Manufacturing, and applying practical principles and techniques wisely (i.e. Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA), Error-Proofing, Quality Circles, Small Improvement Events or Kaizen, or other if / when applicable, or research and develop other innovative solutions.

 Key Job Responsibilities 

 1. Daily Shop Engagement : Go/See the production work areas regularly, attend recurring / standing meetings that communicate operational needs/requirements to assist with daily operational challenges. Examples may include a daily management meeting, a shop walk-through seeking ways to help resolve daily issues, a shift hand-off meeting, maintenance / production / scheduling meetings, a weekly meeting with the Site Manager, etc.

 2.  Create Production Routers : Create / update SAP routers for production work.  This may include a very formal creation of a production router: (a) define the work centers and sequences that the parts must follow in order to produce the product – including outside services if applicable, (b) define work elements at each work center, (c) create appropriate standard work and include tooling/fixturing/jigs needed to optimize the work, and (d) enter the labor and material standards into SAP with labor and material. Most commonly, the router will include a historical time to perform each tasks but still include routing steps and time estimates to establish standard cost.

 3.  Engineering Change Control : With daily interactions, become aware of engineering changes that need clarifications, support production or other departments in engineering revision control, ensure current and accurate data is delivered with inquiries being addressed, delivering answers to the shop with a high sense of urgency to mitigate stalls and delays in production. Follow established process to update manufacturing documents as needed – i.e. drawings, production routers, programs, etc.

Bring insight and solutions to work independently and/or through soliciting feedback from EHS, quality, production, manufacturing, or design engineering. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer II, Autonomous Airpower
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

 The Air Dominance and Strike Division is one of Anduril’s fastest growing, most technically complex divisions. We develop and build collaborative combat aircraft, missiles, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. We are scaling production of autonomous aircraft across our manufacturing facilities. Manufacturing Engineering drives process development, production readiness, and the transition from prototype to rate — ensuring that what Design engineers create can be built reliably, repeatedly, and at scale.

 ABOUT THE JOB 

 Anduril is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer II to join the Autonomous Airpower manufacturing team in Costa Mesa, California. You will own portions of the manufacturing value chain for autonomous aircraft hardware — implementing and refining manufacturing processes to hit production targets and quality standards. This role spans the full breadth of manufacturing engineering disciplines and may focus on one or more of the following areas depending on your background: structures and composites, mechanical systems (landing gear, doors, actuators), fluid systems (hydraulic, fuel, pneumatic), propulsion integration, avionics, or harnessing and electrical integration.

 At this level, you are expected to execute manufacturing engineering projects with moderate supervision, manage your own timelines and priorities, and begin mentoring junior engineers and technicians. You bring solid manufacturing fundamentals, hands-on experience on a production floor, and the ability to analyze workflows, identify bottlenecks, and drive targeted improvements. You are comfortable designing tooling and fixtures, troubleshooting production issues in real time, and translating technical constraints into actionable information for cross-functional partners.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

• Own the manufacturing value chain for assigned aircraft subsystems or assemblies — from process development through work instruction authoring, tooling definition, and production support

• Implement and refine manufacturing processes to achieve production targets and quality standards for your subsystems

• Analyze current workflows to identify bottlenecks and drive targeted cycle time reductions

• Author and maintain work instructions, quality plans, inspection requirements, and manufacturing BOMs that enable technicians to build hardware consistently

• Proficiently utilize CAD software to design tooling, fixtures, and production layouts for aircraft assemblies

• Provide DFM/DFA feedback to design engineering, communicating manufacturing constraints and suggesting alternatives based on hands-on production experience

• Execute assigned manufacturing engineering projects — managing timelines, coordinating with vendors and internal teams, and tracking progress to engineering leadership

• Troubleshoot production issues in real time, developing practical solutions to minimize downtime on the factory floor

• Apply Lean and Six Sigma tools (5S, value stream mapping, FMEA) to specific production areas and lead smaller improvement initiatives

• Mentor junior engineers and technicians, providing guidance on routine assignments and manufacturing best practices

jobs.title: Mechanical Design Engineer, PCB (STARLINK)
jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 MECHANICAL DESIGN ENGINEER, PCB (STARLINK) 

 SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.

 As a Mechanical Design Engineer on Starlink, you will own high impact projects that enable mass production of printed circuit boards. You will design custom tooling and machinery for production processes that range from manual to highly automated. You will own various projects from initial design to installation and mass production.

 Your work will form the backbone for millions of next generation consumer-facing devices that we ship directly to customers and businesses all over the world. From private homes, RVs, planes, or boats, this team plays an instrumental role in leveling the playing field for high-speed connectivity.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Design and develop structures, mechanisms, and automation equipment to enable high volume production of printed circuit boards.

• Demonstrate extreme ownership of projects through their lifecycle, from initial concept generation through fabrication and production bring-up

• Solve complex, open-ended problems with an emphasis on speed and execution and efficiency

• Understand Design of Manufacturability and Assembly specific to PCBs, including panelization, fiducials, keep-out zones, and component placement constraints.

• Develop project plans, budgets, and cost/benefit analysis of implementation of new processes or machines

• Organize project coordination with internal SpaceX resources and external vendors to maintain project timelines and budgets

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline

• 1+ years of experience designing mechanical systems using 3D CAD software, FEA, and 2D drawing. 

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• Prior work experience with structural design and analysis

• Experience with custom machine design, electromechanical systems, motors, actuators, linear rails, bearings, end of arm tooling design, lifting/rigging, etc.

• Strong expertise in design for manufacturability and design for assembly including experience taking products from development to high-volume production.

• Understanding of drafting standards and the application of GD&T

• Experience with Siemens Unigraphics (UGS/NX) and Teamcenter CAD/PDM Systems

• Experience with manufacturing process development, facility and line layouts, process failure mode effects analysis, and error proofing

• Understanding of PCB fabrication and assembly processes

• Experience with mechanical fixturing and automation for high volume PCB lines

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS
