ABOUT ROCKET LAB 

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

 ABOUT THE ROLE 

 Manufacturing Engineering powers Rocket Lab’s factories from concept to full-scale production. We turn early ideas into manufacturable designs, build and optimise the systems that make them real, and constantly push for faster, better, smarter ways to build. We engineer the factories that build the rockets, boosting quality, cutting cost, and accelerating build rate.  

 We're seeking experienced Senior Manufacturing Engineers across multiple disciplines to take ownership of complex products, lead problem-solving initiatives, and drive manufacturing excellence. 

 THE OPPORTUNITIES: 

 We're hiring across four key manufacturing disciplines: 

• Assembly & Integration  – Mechanical, Assembly, Propulsion, Mechanical Test 

• Avionics & Test  – Electronics manufacturing, electrical test, debugging systems 

• Composites  – Advanced materials, resins, ablatives, sandwich structures 

• Machining  – CNC programming, precision manufacturing, GD&T 

 In your application, please indicate which discipline(s) align with your experience and interests. 

 YOU’LL GET TO: 

• Own & Ship: 

• Own products in production as the go-to expert 

• Drive teams to hit production targets at top quality 

• Execute product improvements and design qualifications 

• Solve & Fix: 

• Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions on failures 

• Disposition non-conformances on flight hardware using engineering judgment and risk assessment 

• Bridge production, quality, supply chain, and design engineering for rapid problem-solving 

• Build & Improve: 

• Create bulletproof production procedures and processes 

• Design reliable assemblies and test fixtures 

• Develop mission-critical test methods for safety-critical systems 

• Champion Lean/Six Sigma continuous improvement 

• Lead & Scale: 

• Drive design reviews as DFM/DFT expert 

• Launch new products and revisions into production 

• Plan and execute capital equipment upgrades with business cases 

• Implement planning, quality, ERP, and data systems 

• Mentor & Deliver: 

• Train engineers and production teams 

• Break down complex projects and deliver on time 

• Establish and execute project plans autonomously 

• Maintain product manuals and lessons-learned docs 

 WHAT YOU BRING: 

 The Must-Haves: 

• Engineering degree (Electrical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Chemical, Materials, or related) 

• 5+ years manufacturing/production/process engineering in the trenches 

• Well-tested debugging complex systems on the factory floor 

• You ship results independently and lead teams to do the same 

• You influence stakeholders, assess risk fast, and implement lasting solutions 

• Thrive in high pressure environments – can hustle and built for speed 

 Your Specialty (one or more): 

• Avionics & Test: Expert-level debugging of electro-mechanical systems, instrumentation (oscilloscopes, power supplies, sensors, serial devices) 

• Composites: Deep knowledge of resins, ablatives, sandwich structures, tooling, and manufacturing processes 

• Machining: Advanced GD&T, inspection methods, CAM software (3/5-axis CNC), 3+ years shop experience 

• Assembly & Integration: Led mechanical assembly, integration, propulsion, or mechanical test operations 

 Extra Edge: 

• Aerospace/defence/high-reliability manufacturing background 

• Lean/Six Sigma certified 

• ERP/PLM systems (Siemens TeamCenter, Infor LN) 

• DFMEA, PFMEA, Fault Tree, root cause/corrective action expert 

• SPC, capacity modelling, value stream mapping 

• Environmental testing (vibe, shock, thermal, vacuum) 

• Mentored or led engineers 

 WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU: 

 You own it. Problems become solutions. Documentation gets done. Projects ship on time. You communicate clearly, lead when needed, support teammates always, and show up ready to build the future. 

 We take delivery incredibly seriously. Failure is not in our DNA. The work is hard, demanding, and not for the faint-hearted. 

 You don't go to Mars working eight to five, Monday to Friday. If you're a high performer, hungry for work with genuine impact where your engineering excellence directly shapes space exploration, national security, and critical infrastructure, you've found your place. 

 In return, you'll solve problems that actually matter alongside experts who run toward challenges, not away from them. 

 If this resonates with you, apply today! 
 WHAT TO EXPECT 

 We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. 

 Important information:

 FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY: 

 To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. jobs.desc:
Job Description: 
 Start date: September 2027 
 Location: Broughton 
 Duration: 36 months 

 Application: We love your interest in joining Airbus! There is no limit on the number of positions you can apply for, however, please be aware that you can only progress in the selection process for one position at a time . We recommend reviewing all available opportunities and applying to those that best match your experience and aspirations. 

 Closing date for applications: 15th November 2026 

 Benefits : 
 Salary :   A competitive starting salary of £19,185 
 35 hours per week (on either a standard working day or a double-day shift pattern, providing flexibility) // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays // Pension // Success share // Plus many more flexible benefits! 

 About us: 

 Ready to build the wings that lift the world? Join Airbus as a Craft Tool Room Apprentice in Airbus Broughton and play a vital role in maintaining the  wing jigs and associated Tooling  for our A320, A330, and A350 aircraft families. This 36-month program offers valuable hands-on training, recognised qualifications, and a clear path to a rewarding career in aviation." 

 At Airbus, we believe a diverse workforce drives innovation. We're committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to thrive.  Airbus is a global pioneer in the aerospace industry, leading the way in designing, manufacturing, and delivering aerospace products across Commercial Aircraft, Helicopters, Defence, and Space sectors. 

 As the global center of excellence for wing manufacturing, our Broughton site delivers over 500 wing sets annually. Our apprenticeship programs are carefully designed to give you valuable practical training alongside your academic studies, setting you up for success and helping your career truly fly. 

 With over 17,5000 employees worldwide and as the largest aeronautics and space company in Europe, Airbus is at the forefront of the aviation industry. During your apprenticeship you will work alongside our experienced engineers and quality team to support you to complete the work safely and efficiently 

 What you will be doing: 

 As a Craft Tool Room Apprentice , you'll immerse yourself in hands-on technical experience in the workplace while completing your academic studies. This program is designed to equip you with valuable qualifications and competencies to work directly on live aircraft. You'll also benefit from our Gen A support network and learning HUB , providing additional support, events, and opportunities for all early career participants. 

 This 36-month apprenticeship is structured to maximise your learning and impact: 

 Year One: You will spend the first 12 months of your apprenticeship based at Coleg Cambria, Bersham Road, Wrexham, working towards obtaining: 
 • NVQ L2 diploma in Performing Engineering Operations 
• City & Guild 2850 Level 2 In Machining 
• Level 2 Essential Skills 

 This will allow you to develop the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to enable you to make an immediate contribution when you enter the workforce in the second year. 

 Year 2 and 3:   Your Learning Takes Flight at Broughton! Building on your foundational knowledge, you will be based at Airbus Broughton (North Wales) and you'll join our expert team of multi skilled Tool Makers within the Tool Room area, supporting the manufacture of wing skins, panels and stringers for various Airbus aircraft, working within all the Broughton production areas.  The tasks will be varied,  and will require you to apply your skills directly to live projects,  allowing you to work on the job whilst gaining the relevant skills, knowledge and experience. This will include: 

 • Maintenance of the production jigs / tools, and using a variety of machines within the machine shop: 
• Carrying out routine Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) and reactive breakdown repairs on all Industrial Maintenance assets within the Airbus Broughton plant, completing this to a high competent level and working in a safe and efficient manner.   
• Demonstrate effective troubleshooting on all aspects of plant jigs and tools.   
• Repair & maintain the build jigs and the associated tooling through the use of hand skills, engineering tools and laser trackers (non-contact measurement).  
• Carrying out recertifications to the jigs and tools in order to ensure they meet the design criteria.  
• We also have a machine shop consisting of various machines (both CNC and conventional) that supports the day to day running of the plant and also carrying out non contact (digital) measurements using laser trackers and a Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM).  

 Additionally you will also attend college on day release, working towards gaining: 

 • NVQ Level 3 Extended Diploma in Mechanical Manufacturing Engineering  (Machining Bias units) 
• City & Guilds 2850 Level 3 Machining  

 Upon successful completion of your 36-month apprenticeship, you'll become a Multi skilled Tool maker working within the Tooling Operations  team supporting our world-class Airbus aircraft. You'll receive a Modern Apprenticeship Certificate, setting you up for a fantastic career. 

 Requirements 

 In order to be eligible to this apprenticeship you must: 

 • Achieve a minimum of five GCSEs which must include: 
 • Grade C or 4 in Maths (GCSE certificate only - no equivalency accepted) 
• Grade C or 4 in English Language (GCSE certificate only - no equivalency accepted) 
• Grade CC or 44 in Double Award Science OR Grade C/4 in Single award in Physics. 
• Plus 2 other GCSEs at grade C or 4 (other qualifications that are equivalent or higher may be considered as an alternative to the additional 2 GCSE’s, preferably in a practical or technical subject (e.g., Design & Technology, Engineering, etc) 
• Attach your CV (stating your predicted or achieved grades) and cover letter stating your motivation for the role and industry.

jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

jobs.title: STAGE (6 MOIS) - Stagiaire méthodes industrialisation / amélioration continue - F/H (Bac+5)
jobs.desc:
À la tête des entreprises qui s’engagent vers un avenir plus vert, Alstom développe et commercialise des solutions de mobilité qui apportent les fondements durables pour l'avenir des transports. Notre portefeuille de produits s'étend des trains à grande vitesse, métros, monorails et tramways jusqu’aux systèmes intégrés, services sur mesure, infrastructures, signalisation et solutions de mobilité numérique. Nous rejoindre, c'est rejoindre une entreprise bienveillante, responsable et innovante où plus de 80 000 personnes ouvrent la voie à une mobilité plus verte et plus intelligente, dans le monde entier. Évoluer au sein d’Alstom permet de développer ses compétences, la reconnaissance et d’évoluer dans un contexte international. Nous sommes leader mondial du transport et de la mobilité durable, nous construisons la mobilité de demain. 

 Notre site de Bourgogne (850 salariés), Alstom Le Creusot, est centre d'excellence en matière de conception et fabrication de bogies (châssis, roues, essieux, freins) pour les TGV, trams, trains, métros en France et dans le monde. Le site est situé en plein cœur de Bourgogne, à 1h20 de Paris et 40 min de Lyon (TGV). 

 Nous recrutons un/une Stagiaire Méthodes d'industrialisation/Amélioration Continue - F/H (niveau BAC+3 / BAC+4 / BAC +5).  

 Votre futur rôle 

 Vous mettrez à profit votre expertise en ingénierie des méthodes et en amélioration continue dans un nouveau domaine de pointe. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de production, d'ingénierie et de maintenance, et contribuerez directement à optimiser les opérations de production tout en renforçant l'efficacité des processus industriels. 

 Au quotidien, vous serez amené à : 

• Analyser les processus et flux de production existants pour identifier les opportunités d’amélioration, 

• Proposer et concevoir des solutions innovantes et pratiques en lien avec les principes du Lean Manufacturing , 

• Développer des outillages et équipements mécaniques adaptés pour améliorer les performances opérationnelles , 

• Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de production et le bureau d'études pour assurer la mise en œuvre efficace des solutions proposées, 

• Élaborer des indicateurs de performance pour mesurer l’impact des améliorations apportées, 

• Contribuer à la réduction des gaspillages et à l’optimisation des flux de production, 

• Elaborer des instructions de montage a partir des données du bureau d'études. 

 Votre profil 

 Vous êtes actuellement en formation en génie industriel, mécanique ou dans un domaine connexe (Bac+3 à Bac+5).  Vous avez des connaissances des principes du Lean Manufacturing et êtes familiarisé avec des logiciels de conception mécanique (CATIA, SolidWorks ou équivalent…). 

 Vous êtes motivé par le domaine de l'amélioration continue et les démarches d'innovation industrielle. Vous êtes doté(e) d’un esprit analytique, d’une grande rigueur et d’un excellent sens de l’organisation. Vous démontrez aussi des compétences en communication et un fort esprit d’équipe. Vous êtes polyvalent et vous avez envie de découvrir plusieurs facettes du métier. 

 Chez Alstom, nous accordons plus d'importance à la passion et à l’état d’esprit qu'à l'expérience. C'est pourquoi nous n'attendons pas de vous que vous maitrisez toutes ces compétences mais que vous ayez l'envie de les développer. 

 Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

 Nous valorisons le leadership, la résilience, l’adaptabilité et un état d’esprit d’apprentissage continu. En tant que stagiaire, vous aurez l’opportunité de développer votre expertise dans un environnement stimulant et de contribuer à des projets ayant un impact direct sur nos performances industrielles. 

 Ce que vous apprécierez 

 Nous vous permettrons de vivre une expérience professionnelle au sein d'un secteur d'avenir où vous développerez de nouvelles compétences et expériences qui seront ensuite utiles tout au long de votre carrière. Vous pourrez également : 

• Collaborer avec des équipes transversales et des collègues qualifiés, 

• Contribuer à des projets innovants, 

• Evoluer au sein d'un groupe à renommée mondiale, 

• Participer à la construction des solutions de mobilité durable de demain. 

 Il n'est pas nécessaire d'être un passionné de trains pour s'épanouir chez nous. Nous vous garantissons que lorsque vous monterez dans l'un de nos trains avec vos amis ou votre famille, vous en serez fier. Si vous êtes prêt à relever le défi, nous aimerions vous connaître ! Postulez dès maintenant et devenez acteur/trice de la transformation industrielle chez Alstom ! 
 Alstom garantit l'égalité des chances et s'engage en tant qu’employeur à créer un environnement de travail inclusif où tous sont encouragés à atteindre leur plein potentiel, et où les différences individuelles sont valorisées et respectées. Tous les candidats qualifiés sont considérés dans nos processus de recrutement sans tenir compte de l’origine, de la couleur de peau, de la religion, du sexe, de l'orientation sexuelle, de l'identité de genre, de l'âge, de la nationalité, de la nature du handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la loi locale. 

 Important à noter 

 En tant qu'entreprise mondiale, nous sommes un employeur qui prône l'égalité des chances et qui célèbre la diversité dans les 63 pays où nous sommes présents. Nous nous engageons à créer un lieu de travail inclusif pour tous

jobs.title: Advanced Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
ABOUT APTIV 

 At Aptiv, we are shaping the future of mobility by developing technologies that make transportation safer, greener, and more connected. Our teams collaborate across engineering, manufacturing, and product development to deliver innovative solutions for the world’s leading automotive manufacturers.

 The North American Connection Systems team is at the forefront of developing advanced manufacturing technologies and processes that transform product concepts into scalable, high-quality production solutions. If you are passionate about hands-on engineering, innovation, and solving complex manufacturing challenges, we invite you to join us.

 YOUR ROLE 

 We are seeking an Advanced Manufacturing Engineer to join our team at the Champion Technical Center in Warren, Ohio .

 In this role, you will work closely with Product Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, and Supplier partners to develop and industrialize new products from prototype through full-scale production. You will play a key role in designing manufacturing processes, developing tooling and fixturing, and introducing innovative technologies that improve product quality, efficiency, and scalability.
 This is an excellent opportunity for an engineer who enjoys a hands-on environment, thrives on problem solving, and is passionate about bringing new products and manufacturing technologies to life.

 HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE 

 You will partner with cross-functional teams across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain to develop robust manufacturing solutions that support both new product launches and continuous improvement initiatives.

 In your daily work, you will: 

 • Develop manufacturing processes for new products from prototype through serial production.

• Design, develop, and implement tooling and fixturing solutions to support product development and manufacturing activities.

• Lead advanced manufacturing projects focused on improving existing processes, equipment, and production methods.

• Identify and incorporate leading-edge manufacturing technologies into Aptiv products and operations.

• Create and maintain work instructions, process documentation, lessons learned, and project status updates.

• Develop manufacturing process estimates and contribute to Statements of Work (SOWs) for product industrialization activities.

• Collaborate with engineering teams, manufacturing plants, and suppliers to ensure successful project execution.

• Drive supplier activities, technical requirements, and project timelines to support launch objectives.

• Utilize data-driven analysis to support engineering decisions and process improvements.

• Ensure compliance with customer-specific requirements, internal quality standards, and manufacturing best practices.

• Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, efficiency, and cost optimization.

 KEY SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS 

 To be successful in this role, you should bring: 

 • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering Technology, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related discipline.

• 1-2 years of experience building, improving, repairing, or developing manufacturing equipment, fixtures, or processes.

• 1-2 years of experience working within a manufacturing environment and collaborating with cross-functional teams.

• Strong problem-solving skills and a passion for innovation and continuous improvement.

• Ability to visualize manufacturing processes and understand component interactions.

• Experience using CAD software such as SolidWorks, Solid Edge, AutoCAD, NX, or similar design tools.

• Ability to translate ideas into technical concepts, CAD models, prototypes, and production-ready solutions.

• Strong analytical, organizational, and project execution skills.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Ability to work effectively with individuals at all levels of the organization.

• Self-motivated, adaptable, and capable of thriving in a fast-paced environment.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 Experience in one or more of the following areas is highly desirable: 

 • CAM software such as Mastercam, Trumpf TruTops, or similar platforms.

• Automated manufacturing equipment design and implementation.

• Ultrasonic welding technologies.

• Laser cutting and laser welding processes.

• Electrical connector component design or assembly processes.

• Design for Manufacturing (DFM) methodologies.

• Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA).

• Advanced manufacturing automation and industrialization projects.

• Microsoft Office applications including Excel, Project, Outlook, Word, and Teams.

 Position Summary 
 We are seeking a skilled and motivated Manufacturing Engineer with CNC machining experience to support our manufacturing operations and drive continuous improvement initiatives. This position is responsible for developing, implementing, and optimizing CNC machining processes to improve productivity, quality, safety, and cost performance. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in CNC machining, process development, tooling, fixture design, and lean manufacturing principles.

 · Experience with cutting tools, tooling selection, fixturing, and process optimization.
 · Understanding of GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing) and engineering drawings.
 · Experience with root cause analysis and continuous improvement methodologies.
 · Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
 · Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
 · Excellent communication and teamwork abilities.
 Preferred Qualifications

 · Familiarity with Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Okuma, or similar CNC controls.
 · Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and Kaizen methodologies.
 · Experience with APQP, PPAP, PFMEA, Control Plans, and SPC.
 · Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
 · Experience with automation, robotics, and Industry 4.0 technologies.
 · Knowledge of ISO 9001 and/or IATF 16949 quality systems.
 Physical Requirements 
 · Ability to work in a manufacturing environment around machining equipment and moving machinery.
 · Ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift up to 25 pounds occasionally.

 · Ability to travel occasionally as needed.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
Join Komatsu and Be Part of Something Big! 
 Job Overview 

 Complete in a timely manner Manufacturing Engineering related projects with emphasis on safe work practices, Production/Warehouse Department procedures, routings, packaging requirements, manpower requirements, standards, layout, tooling/fixtures, equipment purchases that provide method improvements and cost reduction opportunities. Projects will include improved process flow in the fabrication/warehouse through shipping operations as well as supporting material flow and systems from suppliers to line side delivery. Programming CNC machines, fabricating, welding, painting, and assembly part knowledge with experience to develop processes to produce a part per print. Understand all warehouse processes through inbound packaging, put away, picking, packing, and shipping. Purpose of this position is to support and foster continuous improvement of all aspects of the Production/Warehouse Process. 

 Recommends tooling, equipment and system purchases to support current and new models along with warehouse processing of spare parts.  

 Responsible for generating routings, procedures, tool specifications and programs for automated equipment to meet SQDC demands. 

 Review layouts for continuous improvement and develop standards for all processes with manufacturing and warehouse operations.  

 Key Job Responsibilities 

 Select tools and programs related to automated equipment, such as CNC machine tools by utilizing CAD/CAM and computer software to effectively utilize manpower, machines, and facilities. 

 Complete projects assigned timely by utilizing project planning tools and communicating with all aspects required to successfully complete each project. 

 Recommends tooling, equipment to assist Fabrication and Warehousing through confirmation process flow for existing Models and revised and/or new Models along with warehouse processes. 

 Update Production routings to coordinate fabrication through assembly flow, include confirmation and report proper costing and coordinate introduction of ECN’s (Engineering Change Notices). Setup operations within MRP system to manage inventory for warehouse. 

 Develop Manpower requirements for area assigned of the Production Department to support changing production volumes and assist with proper manning levels. Including Warehouse Department.

Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Propulsion Manufacturing Integrated Components team manufactures and tests critical Aeon-R engine components including manifolds, gimbal assemblies, brackets, orifices, etc. The team ensures on-time delivery of propulsion subassemblies to the Aeon-R engine program while driving continuous improvements in safety, quality, reliability, lead time, and cost. 

 After successfully delivering hardware and developing processes for the first Aeon-R flight engines, we're entering a critical phase: ramping production while concurrently developing next-generation engines to make Terran R the most manufacturable high-performing rocket to date. This role requires a high degree of autonomy and initiative to provide design feedback, pioneer advanced manufacturing methods, and deliver flight hardware for integration and testing. 

 About the Role: 

• Own and develop manufacturing and test processes for 3D printed and machined Aeon-R engine components and subassemblies 

• Drive continuous improvements in manufacturability, assembly, and delivery of components, ensuring hardware meets all aspects of the intended design 

• Collaborate with manufacturing partners and technicians by writing work instructions, conducting root cause analysis, resolving issues, and tracking and reducing lead time 

• Partner with supply chain to develop and manage external supplier relationships, ensuring on-time hardware delivery 

• Work hands-on in a fast-paced, often novel, high-mix environment while collaborating cross-functionally and driving projects to completion 

• Build a strong manufacturing team and lead projects directly and cross-functionally 

 About You: 

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field and 2+ years of relevant experience in manufacturing engineering or a related role. 

• Strong foundational knowledge of propulsion systems, mechanics of materials, and thermal-fluid systems to investigate and resolve hardware defects 

• Ability to work with and train technicians in a hands-on hardware environment, writing work instructions, and process plans for complex assemblies, and drive implementation of improvement and corrective actions 

• Vendor management experience including selection, defect disposition, and quality management 

• Proficiency with additive/subtractive manufacturing, precision inspection, GD&T (ASME Y14.5), and FEA using Ansys or similar tools 

• Experience with tooling design using Siemens NX or other CAD tools, including conceptualization, modeling, analysis, and fabrication 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Experience in propulsion development programs 

• Experience transitioning products from development to high-volume production 

• Hands-on experience with CNC machining, welding, and high-pressure testing 

• Experience writing formal process specifications and manufacturing standards

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

The Cape is the only place where you see it all come together, offering a level of exposure and responsibility unmatched elsewhere in the program. This is where first flights happen, where history is built on top of history, and where the scale of what's underway is unlike anything in modern aerospace. The mission stays the same, but the work evolves with every milestone: from first launch to reuse, high-cadence operations, and beyond. If you're looking to define what's next in space launch and write a new playbook, not just repeat what’s already been done, this is where it happens.

 In this role, you will work closely with Test and Launch design engineers to evaluate and implement optimal manufacturing and integration solutions. You will lead fabrication and integration efforts, including coordination with third-party vendors and full ownership of integration processes. You’ll collaborate with cross-functional teams—including fluids, civil, electrical, and mechanical disciplines—to develop effective integration strategies. You'll also be responsible for selecting techniques and processes that meet design tolerances, while providing input on and approving designs for manufacturability.

• 2+ years of experience supporting manufacturing activities related to structural builds, precision tooling, ground support equipment, or similar hardware.

• Experience with mechanical systems, mechanisms, or moving assemblies. 

• Experience checking engineering drawings and reviewing geometric dimensioning and tolerancing standards.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 PROCESS ENGINEER (STARSHIP) 

 As a Process Engineer with a focus on Starship build reliability, you will be part of a widely interdisciplinary team developing global manufacturing procedures, maximizing quality through efficient production. You will employ “reliability by any means necessary”, stretching your expertise in fabrication methods, work instructions, tooling design, inspection procedures, data gathering/visualization, and broad collaboration. You will build new processes from the ground up, and routinely grade/improve execution of existing processes, driving continuous production improvement and ultimately be responsible for build-induced vehicle risk.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Develop manufacturing, integration, assembly, welding, NDE, cleanliness, and checkouts processes from the ground up, then enforce consistency across different work centers.

• Design and implement tooling for work access, mechanical/avionics/propulsion testing, build fixturing, lifting & rigging, and fluids.

• Define and document inspection requirements and procedures.

• Create training for production and inspection processes.

• Author planning, test plans, and training to execute processes and collect data, ensuring efficient and stable quality at increasing production volumes.

• Contain non-conforming hardware in collaboration with quality, production, and design groups to ensure systemic issues are corrected, and risk is managed for the fleet.

• Work closely with design teams to improve DFM and requirement fulfillment. Aggressively modify requirements and manufacturing process where design intent and production rate are incompatible.

• Conduct build quality reviews to identify repeat and high impact issues. Drive corrective action within and outside of your work center.

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, materials engineering, manufacturing engineering, chemical engineering, electrical engineering, or engineering physics.

• 1+ years in manufacturing, quality, and/or design engineering role (student project team or internship experience qualifies).

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• Experience with the build, assembly, or integration of structures, avionics, valves, fluid system components, actuators, thermal protection systems, or other aerospace components.

• Mechanical tooling or component design and design for manufacturability.

• Proficiency with 3D CAD Software such as NX, SolidWorks, or CATIA.

• Knowledge of mig, tig, laser, stud, spot, or robot welding techniques, as well as visual, penetrant, x-ray, EMAT, or other NDT processes.

• Involvement in a collegiate or hobby design project (Formula SAE, rocketry, etc).

• Proficiency with SQL and Power BI or other database/query/data visualization suite.

• You thrive in a hands-on environment and are hungry to step out of the office, onto the shop floor.

• Knowledge of metallic manufacturing techniques, processes, and equipment related to machining, bending, forming, casting, additive manufacturing, fastening, drilling, and/or bonding.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 SR. PROCESS ENGINEER – WAFER LEVEL ASSEMBLY, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND) 

 SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.

 The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Sr. Process Engineer on the Starmind team, you’ll have ownership over the entire life-cycle of the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. Your work sits at the intersection of process, packaging, materials, and thermal engineering. The Payload team is responsible for the design of industry-leading compute electronics, memory, and networking in order to achieve required domain sizes and processing workloads.

• Own the full lifecycle of advanced packaging through board assembly process development— including requirements capture, materials selection, prototyping, process optimization, manufacturing, and failure analysis.

• Own the full lifecycle of equipment specification, qualification, and ramp.

• Build supply chains for die, packages, components, consumable chemicals, and equipment for satellite compute manufacturing. Define incoming acceptance criteria for components and materials.

• Specify and implement in-process metrology tools for quality control. Integrate simulation tools with experimental data to guide and drive targeted process improvements.

• Drive end-to-end process R&D programs, from concept through product implementation, to drive cost down, efficiency improvements, and reliability in electronic systems.

• Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, materials, electrical, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware

• Challenge assumptions, question requirements, learn from your mistakes, and approach problems with an open mind

jobs.title: Satellite AIT Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
Job Description: 
 As a Thermo-Mechanical AIT ME (Manufacturing Engineer) you will be assigned to one of the Space System Business Lines (Earth Observation Science & Exploration, Telecom& Nav System, Constellation), and given assignment to specific set of projects, managed transversally by a Lead Project Manager. You will get integrated as ME active workforce inside a multi-Functional project team, where all members receive the challenge to successfully develop, industrialize, produce and deliver a finished and fully functional product to an end customer in the Space sector.
 Spacecraft Production Spain comprises a set of well-established Space products in Airbus Space Systems portfolio, devoted to Earth Observation Science & Exploration (i.e Paz 2, Copernicus LSTM, Aeolus2, METOP SAS & ICI), Telecomm & Nav Systems Programs (i.e. Adler, SpainSat, Galileo) and potentially to Constellation Programs.
 Purpose of Thermo-Mechanical AIT Process Engineer is to enable, for the project(s) he is assigned to the implementation of the Manufacturing System in the relevant AIT domains as follows:
 • Thermo-mechanical assembly and integration of Spacecraft (S/C) instruments and payload

• Electrical hardware integration on instruments and payload

• Test Set up and de-set up

• Payload / System mechanical integration into Spacecraft

• Satellite final integration

• Handling, loading and shipping of payload / satellite

 RESPONSIBILITIES 
 This translates into the following main accountabilities:
 • Concur with Engineering domains during development phase so to ensure Design solution is feasible and fits the industrial system.

• Bringing industrial incomes and expertise to multifunctional teams assigned to projects.

• Gain proper awareness and understanding of the whole configured set of Engineering technical information applicable for elaborating the Manufacturing Dossier in the project, so due traceability is granted (As Design-As Planned)

• Analyzing and optimizing manufacturing technologies and capabilities available in Space Spain Plant or at extended industrial partners & suppliers.

• Ensure the feasibility of Assembly Integration and Testing of the thermal, mechanical and electrical hardware.

• Ensure Material & Processes Selection List and Standard Selection List in the Manufacturing Dossier all fit in the AIT execution works allocated in the project.

• Define the Manufacturing Bill of Material (MBOM) and make material requirements available to the Supply Chain.

• Technically support project AIT manager & Production staff during shopfloor execution of breadboards, Qualification and Flight Models. This may include on-site assistance to customer sites or spaceports during launch campaigns or supplier facilities for environmental, RF or mechanical test campaigns.

• Build process definition for AIT activities in the project, this includes:
 • Defining the as planned structure in concurrence with Engineering & Mechanical Design Office.

• Characterize the AIT work sequence and key industrial parameters iaw Airbus OES guidelines (i.e process flow, process time, lead time, critical path, skills mapping, white spaces, …)

• Identify the need and specify requirements for industrial asset (Jigs, Tools, Tooling, Machines, …).

• Integrate the Quality inputs relevant to the AIT activities (Control Plan) to ensure conformity of the product

• Consider inputs from PFMEA and Health & Safety general regulation as well as local counsel H&S advise.

• Schedule and delivery rates constrains.

• Resources and Means optimization.

• Economic aspects.

 • Lead the work preparation activities in the project(s) i.e. release Systems Mechanical&Electrical Integration Procedures and incorporate them into comprehensive Work Orders, iaw the build process layout.

• Foster regular feedback loops with the Production & Quality Team

• Support shop floor continuous improvement by providing rational and conclusions based on work prep expertise and takeaways from lessons learned exercises, PPS, etc…

• Provide technical advice in the budget preparation, sometimes involved in CapEx planning to support determination of cost improvement measures.

• Developing and deploying capability in case of New Product / Process is introduced. This includes support and influence on qualification campaigns along with Material & Process and Design Dpts.

 SKILLS 
 • Aerospace, Telecommunications, Industrial or Mechanical Engineering.

• From 3 to 5 years of experience in the AIT (Assembly integration and Test) production field, preferably in AIT Space or in Manufacturing Engineering.

• Nice to have:
 • Knowledge of ESA standards (ECSSs)

• Knowledge of CATIA

• Knowledge of DDMS environment (Delmia, Apriso, etc)

• Fluent in English and Spanish language

 At Airbus we are focused on our employees and their welfare. Take a look at some of our social benefits:

jobs.title: Concepteur Bogie / CAD
jobs.desc:
Req ID: 519638  

 Chez Alstom, nous avons une connaissance pointue des réseaux de transport et comprenons ce qui conduit les individus à les emprunter. Des trains à grande vitesse, métros, monorails et tramways aux systèmes intégrés, services, infrastructures, et solutions de signalisation et de mobilité numérique, nous offrons à la diversité de nos clients le portefeuille le plus vaste du secteur.  Chaque jour, plus de 80 000 collaborateurs dans le monde qui ouvrent la voie à des solutions de mobilité plus vertes et plus intelligentes pour relier les villes, réduire l’empreinte carbone et remplacer la voiture.

 Pourriez-vous être le  Concepteur Bogie / CAD  à temps plein à St-Bruno (QC), Canada, que nous recherchons ?

 Votre futur rôle 

 Relevez un nouveau défi et mettez à profit votre expertise en conception mécanique et modélisation 3D dans un environnement stimulant et collaboratif. Vous travaillerez avec une équipe dynamique, innovante et engagée, et vous jouerez un rôle clé dans le développement et la validation des bogies, des composants essentiels pour nos solutions de mobilité durable.

 Au quotidien, vous collaborerez étroitement avec les responsables techniques bogie (PrEM), les équipes de conception, ainsi que les ateliers des ensembliers afin d’assurer la qualité et la fiabilité de nos produits. Vous participerez activement à la réalisation de revues de produit, à la création de modèles 3D et à la rédaction de spécifications techniques, tout en contribuant à l’amélioration continue de nos processus.

 Vous vous occuperez plus particulièrement de la conception et de la validation des bogies, mais aussi de la gestion des objets techniques et des nomenclatures associées.

• 
 Nous ferons appel à vous pour :

• 
 Réaliser des revues de faisabilité des bogies en phase d’offre, en collaboration avec les responsables techniques.

• 
 Créer et gérer des modèles 3D (CATIA V5) et des nomenclatures de définition.

• 
 Réaliser des plans techniques précis et les vérifier.

• 
 Dimensionner les composants à partir de calculs préliminaires.

• 
 Rédiger des spécifications techniques détaillées.

• 
 Participer à la préparation des réponses techniques pour les appels d’offres.

• 
 Assurer le suivi des essais et garantir la qualité des interfaces entre les différents composants.

• 
 Collaborer avec les ateliers des ensembliers et participer à des réunions de suivi pour garantir la conformité des produits.

 Votre profil 

 Nous accordons plus d'importance à la passion et à l’état d’esprit qu'à l'expérience. C'est pourquoi nous n'attendons pas de vous que vous possédiez toutes les compétences. Nous avons plutôt dressé une liste de celles qui, selon nous, vous aideront à réussir et à vous épanouir dans ce rôle :

• 
 Diplôme d’études collégiales (DEC) technique ou baccalauréat en mécanique.

• 
 Bonne connaissance en mécanique générale et technologie.

• 
 Expérience souhaitée de 5 ans dans un poste similaire.

• 
 Maîtrise des logiciels de conception 3D CAD, en particulier CATIA V5.

• 
 Connaissance des notions en conception à coût objectif.

• 
 Notions en fabrication (mécano-soudure, usinage, conception de pièces moulées et forgées).

• 
 Compréhension de la résistance des matériaux.

• 
 Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles, rigueur, autonomie, flexibilité et capacité à respecter les délais.

• 
 Bilinguisme (français et anglais) requis. La maîtrise d’une troisième langue est un atout.

 Ce que vous apprécierez Rejoignez-nous pour une nouvelle expérience de vie - le secteur ferroviaire est un secteur d’avenir, vous pouvez donc vous développer et acquérir de nouvelles compétences et expériences tout au long de votre carrière. Vous pourrez également :

• 
 Bénéficier de stabilité, de défis et d'une carrière à long terme sans routine quotidienne.

• 
 Travailler avec des experts techniques et des professionnels passionnés par l’innovation et la durabilité.

• 
 Collaborer avec des équipes transversales et des collègues qualifiés à l’échelle mondiale.

• 
 Contribuer à des projets innovants qui façonnent l’avenir des transports.

• 
 Utiliser notre environnement de travail flexible et axé sur la collaboration.

• 
 Orienter votre carrière dans la direction de votre choix à travers les fonctions et les pays.

• 
 Bénéficier de notre investissement dans votre développement, par le biais de programmes d’apprentissage primés.

• 
 Progresser vers des rôles de leadership ou d’expertise technique selon vos aspirations.

• 
 Bénéficier d'un système de rémunération équitable et dynamique qui reconnaît vos performances et votre potentiel, ainsi que d'une couverture sociale complète et compétitive (assurance-vie, assurance-maladie, pension).

 La connaissance d'une autre langue que le français est un atout pour faciliter les échanges avec nos partenaires, fournisseurs, collègues et clients internationaux. Au Québec, le français reste la langue de travail principale de notre entreprise.

 Il n’y a pas que les passionnés de trains qui s’épanouissent chez nous. Nul doute que vous ressentirez beaucoup de fierté lorsque vous monterez dans l’un de nos trains avec votre famille ou vos amis. Si vous aimez le challenge, nous serions ravis d’échanger avec vous !

 Remarque importante 

 En tant qu’employeur présent dans plus de 63 pays, nous souscrivons au principe d’égalité d’accès à l’emploi et valorisons la diversité. Nous nous sommes engagés à créer un environnement de travail inclusif pour tous.

About Lucid 

 At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience. 

 We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility. 

 About the Team

 The General Assembly Advanced Manufacturing Engineering team enables Lucid to launch safe, efficient, production-ready assembly processes at scale. The team partners across Product Design, Quality, Operations, Maintenance, Facilities, Supply Chain, and external suppliers to translate vehicle requirements into capable manufacturing equipment and tooling. This group is unique in its end-to-end ownership of equipment strategy, supplier execution, validation, installation, commissioning, and operational handoff, giving team members direct visibility into how engineering decisions affect quality, throughput, safety, and launch readiness.

 About the Role

 The Manufacturing Engineer II is an individual contributor role within General Assembly Advanced Manufacturing Engineering and reports to a Manufacturing Engineering leader. This role exists to support Lucid’s growth by strengthening equipment procurement, integration, validation, and launch readiness for General Assembly programs. In the first 12 months, this person will own assigned equipment and tooling projects from scope development through validated production handoff, with success measured by safe installation, capable processes, clear documentation, on-time issue closure, and readiness for Operations ownership. A strong candidate will gain hands-on accountability across the full manufacturing equipment lifecycle, including supplier technical alignment, factory and site acceptance, launch troubleshooting, and lessons learned that directly shape future high-volume EV production systems.

 What You Own

• 
 Equipment Strategy: Define equipment and tooling scopes, technical specifications, and RFQ packages that align safety, quality, cycle time, throughput, maintainability, timing, and cost requirements before supplier award.

• 
 Supplier Alignment: Evaluate supplier proposals, lead technical clarification, and partner with Purchasing to support supplier selection, purchase-order execution, commercial alignment, and on-time delivery.

•

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer, Connected Warfare
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE SITE 

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1 , its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 The Connected Warfare team focused on the modernization of the command and control systems of U.S. and Allied forces. New technologies and new adversaries demand a new approach to battlefield intelligence, and our products are rapidly scaling in production to deliver the volumes that our customers need. As an Manufacturing Engineer you will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1 , our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. This team will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for 3 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 This role is about much more than just processes; it's about orchestrating the industrialization of a vital product. You will own the entire manufacturing value-chain, from current rate to high-volume deployment. Your responsibilities will span the spectrum: driving Design for Manufacturability (DFM) feedback into design, innovating tool design and selection, creating and optimizing high-rate production lines, fostering strategic vendor partnerships, embedding robust quality assurance throughout, and meticulously documenting build processes.

If you thrive under the pressure of scaling a critical product with immediate, real-world impact, we want you to help us build the next generation of Connected Warfare products.

**This role requires new hires to temporarily work in Costa Mesa, CA for a week or two at a time during the first three months on this job in order to view our operations there. Housing, transportation, etc. will be provided for these short travel periods. You will still be in Ohio during weeks when you're not in CA during this time. After the first few months, you will work mostly in Ashville, OH. 

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Execute the manufacturing of a certain product or set of products, from initial prototyping through large full-scale production.

• Work with design engineers during the development process to drive design for manufacturing best practices into the design effort, and help facilitate the transition from design to prototype to rate production.

• Act as a manufacturing liaison for mechanical fabrication and avionics with subject matter expertise in these areas and key experience in design for manufacturability.

• Own documentation required for successfully manufacturing product group hardware at scale, such as MBOM’s, work instructions, and process flows, etc.

• Advise on quality management and business application programs as they pertain to manufacturing within your area.

• Collaborate with internal customers and manufacturing planning teams to define capacity planning actions to meet customer needs and expectations.

• Analyze metrics for continuous improvement initiatives (cost reduction, QI reduction & capacity increase).

• Instill a culture of innovation, teamwork, and accountability within the manufacturing engineering product team.

• Develop production and test methodologies and implement best practices to enable scaling production capabilities for larger, more complex products.

• Travel to suppliers and partner sites to do initial sourcing work, solve ongoing production issues, and implement process procedures as required.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Degree in a technical field preferred such as engineering, math, or a hard science.

• 1-5 years of experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing or design of electromechanical hardware.

• Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment.

• An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.

• A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning.

• Candidates must demonstrate flexibility and dedication, being prepared to work extended hours and weekends when dictated by critical business priorities.

• Regular travel between our various locations is an essential component of this role.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret Clearance.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• Exposure to aircraft programs or other relevant aerospace & defense technologies.

• Software scripting experience in any language.

• Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) or equivalent experience.

• Familiarity with J-STD-001, IPC-A-610, and IPC/WHMA-A-620 or equivalent standards.

 US Salary Range
 $86,000 — $147,000 USD

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer, Structures and Mechanical Integration, Space
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE ROLE

 Anduril’s Space Manufacturing team is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer for Structures and Mechanical Integration to join our team. Your expertise will help ensure that our products meet the highest standards of quality and reliability at Anduril. 

 As the Manufacturing Engineer for Structures and Mechanical Integration, you will bring deep mechanical and structural engineering experience to the design of the tooling and mechanical ground support equipment (MGSE) our structures and vehicle lines depend on — lifting and handling fixtures, rotation and integration stands, and transport fixtures — while developing and executing the mechanical integration processes that build our spacecraft. You will work hands-on with technicians on the floor. 

 The ideal candidate is a hands-on mechanical/structural manufacturing engineer who has designed MGSE and tooling for flight or comparably high-consequence hardware, and who has taken vehicle-level or major-assembly integration from development into production in a fast-paced environment.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Design and develop mechanical ground support equipment (MGSE) and tooling — lifting and handling fixtures, rotation and integration stands, transport and shipping fixtures — that the structures and vehicle integration lines depend on.

• Perform load-path and structural-margin checks on MGSE and tooling, defining factors of safety and coordinating proof-load and qualification testing before equipment is released for use on flight hardware.

• Develop and qualify mechanical/structural integration processes — precision fastening and torque control, bonded and shimmed joints, mechanism and module installation, and alignment to metrology-defined datums.

• Author and maintain work instructions, travelers, and as-built records for the structural and mechanical build.

• Drive Design for Manufacturability and Assembly into structural and vehicle-level designs before CDR — access, fastener reach, tool clearance, and integration order.

• Own cleanroom manufacturing practice on your line — contamination control, FOD prevention, gowning and material flow across ISO 7 and ISO 5 environments.

• Lead root cause analysis and corrective action for nonconformances; support PFMEA, process validation, and first article inspection.

• Act as an owner and evangelist for Anduril's Manufacturing Development Process (MDP), and use Foundry and Teamcenter as the system of record for build definition, work instructions, and as-built records.

• Support design reviews (PDR, CDR) and manufacturing readiness reviews, and provide hands-on technical support to integration technicians on the floor.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Structural, Manufacturing, or Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• 5+ years of manufacturing or mechanical engineering experience in aerospace, space, defense, or another high-reliability industry, including hands-on work on structural and mechanical assemblies.

• 3+ years designing tooling, fixtures, or mechanical ground support equipment (MGSE) — such as lifting and handling fixtures, rotation and integration stands, and transport fixtures — with attention to load paths, structural margins, and factors of safety, including proof-load or qualification testing of lifting and handling equipment.

• Proficiency with 3D CAD (e.g., Siemens NX) for mechanical/structural design of tooling and MGSE, including GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis.

• Willing to work on-site, with travel up to 15% to development, test, and supplier sites.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Structural analysis background — hand calculations or FEA for GSE and tooling load cases.

• Weight and balance or mass-properties verification and final mechanical close-out operations.

• A quantified cycle-time, yield, or throughput improvement on an assembly or integration line.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 MANUFACTURING ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND) 

 SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high-performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference. 

 The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Manufacturing Engineer on the Starmind team, you’ll have ownership over the entire manufacturing line for the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. Your work spans the assembly, integration, and testing of industry-leading compute electronics, memory, and networking in order to achieve required domain sizes and processing workloads. 

 RESPONSIBILITIES 

• Own the development and optimization of high-rate manufacturing for satellite   

• Own the full lifecycle of equipment specification, validation, and process development— including device modeling, characterization of performance metrics, and materials failure analysis.  

• Build supply chains for wafers, gases, chemicals, and equipment for solar cell manufacturing. Define incoming acceptance criteria for materials (e.g. silicon wafers, conductive pastes).  

• Address material and process challenges in panel-level packaging while spearheading the development of next-generation dielectric materials to improve packaging performance and scalability.  

• Specify and implement in-process metrology tools for quality control. Design wafer-level test structures to evaluate material/electronic properties. Integrate simulation tools with experimental data to guide and drive targeted improvements via material or process changes.  

• Drive end-to-end material and process R&D programs, from concept through product implementation, to drive cost down, efficiency improvements, and reliability in electronic systems.  

• Collaborate closely with leadership and stakeholders across all departments—including design, reliability, production, and supply chain—to integrate materials innovations into product roadmaps and ensure accountability for operations and reliability.  

• Manage compliance risks related to materials and processes, ensuring safety and environmental compliance with industry standards.  

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:     

• Bachelor's degree in an engineering degree.  

• Experience in microelectronics device research or manufacturing.  

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:     

• Internship, co-op, or early-career experience in hardware, robotics, automation, or manufacturing environments  

• Experience designing tooling, fixtures, or jigs for assembly or test applications  

• Exposure to scripting or data analysis tools (e.g., Python, MATLAB, or equivalent) for process data analysis or automation  

• Experience working with precision assemblies, robotic systems, or automated pick-and-place equipment  

• Familiarity with manufacturing process development methodologies (e.g., PFMEA, process capability studies, SPC)  

• Exposure to GD&T and tolerance analysis as applied to fixture and tooling design  

• Experience with or interest in production data systems, MES, or manufacturing traceability infrastructure  

• Familiarity with cleanroom or controlled-environment manufacturing practices  

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:  

• Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines

jobs.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer, Integrated Components
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Propulsion Manufacturing Integrated Components team manufactures and tests critical Aeon-R engine components including manifolds, gimbal assemblies, brackets, orifices, etc. The team ensures on-time delivery of propulsion subassemblies to the Aeon-R engine program while driving continuous improvements in safety, quality, reliability, lead time, and cost. 

 After successfully delivering hardware and developing processes for the first Aeon-R flight engines, we're entering a critical phase: ramping production while concurrently developing next-generation engines to make Terran R the most manufacturable high-performing rocket to date. This role requires a high degree of autonomy and initiative to provide design feedback, pioneer advanced manufacturing methods, and deliver flight hardware for integration and testing. 

 About the Role: 

• Own and develop manufacturing and test processes for 3D printed and machined Aeon-R engine components and subassemblies 

• Drive continuous improvements in manufacturability, assembly, and delivery of components, ensuring hardware meets all aspects of the intended design 

• Collaborate with manufacturing partners and technicians by writing work instructions, conducting root cause analysis, resolving issues, and tracking and reducing lead time 

• Partner with supply chain to develop and manage external supplier relationships, ensuring on-time hardware delivery 

• Work hands-on in a fast-paced, often novel, high-mix environment while collaborating cross-functionally and driving projects to completion 

• Build a strong manufacturing team and lead projects directly and cross-functionally 

 About You: 

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field and 5+ years of relevant experience in manufacturing engineering or a related role. 

• Strong foundational knowledge of propulsion systems, mechanics of materials, and thermal-fluid systems to investigate and resolve hardware defects 

• Ability to work with and train technicians in a hands-on hardware environment, writing work instructions, and process plans for complex assemblies, and drive implementation of improvement and corrective actions 

• Vendor management experience including selection, defect disposition, and quality management 

• Proficiency with additive/subtractive manufacturing, precision inspection, GD&T (ASME Y14.5), and FEA using Ansys or similar tools 

• Experience with tooling design using Siemens NX or other CAD tools, including conceptualization, modeling, analysis, and fabrication 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Experience in propulsion development programs 

• Experience transitioning products from development to high-volume production 

• Hands-on experience with CNC machining, welding, and high-pressure testing 

• Experience writing formal process specifications and manufacturing standards

jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Tooling and Factory Automation team sits at the intersection of design, manufacturing, and automation, making everything from large-scale structural fixtures to small tools that directly enable Terran R’s production. As a design group embedded within the manufacturing organization, we dig deep into the needs of our internal partners to understand root problems, propose solutions, and deliver hardware to help build faster, scale smarter, and work better. The team is also at the forefront of Relativity’s growing factory automation efforts, an increasingly critical part of scaling production of Terran R at existing and future facilities. You’ll have the autonomy to make decisions, field solutions, and see them in action on the factory floor. Ultimately, you’re not just designing tools or automated processes; you’re defining how rockets and factories get built. 

 About the Role: 

 The Mechanical Design Engineers are responsible for the design and development of tools and factory automation equipment that support manufacturing. The Mechanical Engineering team works closely with Design and Manufacturing, turning top-level requirements and concepts into functional delivered equipment. The Mechanical Design Engineering team brings a high level of innovation and ingenuity into the design process, as they are tasked with building out a highly automated production facility. 

• Develop high quality development and production tooling and automation solutions for the Terran vehicle and Aeon engine programs 

• Capable of integrating concepts and principles of mechanical design and analysis of several different projects in a fast-paced environment - projects will vary in size and scale 

• Ability to interpret and apply sound design and drafting standards (ASME Y14.5) in creating tooling drawing definitions 

• Handle a wide range of technical problems and familiar with all types of material handling, assembly fixtures, off-loaders, rotisseries, test fixtures, structural weldments, environmental chambers, and custom machines 

• Close collaboration with component designers, manufacturing engineers, and integration engineering to achieve the best possible cradle to grave metrics (safety, cost, quality, cycle time, delivery, reliability, life, and maintenance/refurbishment) 

• Manage projects including vendor selection, fabrication, inspection, equipment installation, and commissioning of tooling 

 About You: 

• Bachelor of Science degree in manufacturing engineering, mechanical engineering or equivalent 

• 10+ years of work or project experience with design, build, and commissioning of tooling and fixtures for manufacturing, assembly and test 

• Experience using CAD and FEA-based analysis software (NX and ANSYS Workbench preferred) for structural applications 

• Experience in full-cycle project completion 

• Experience in strategic buildout and project management of tooling supporting production 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Strong expertise in design for manufacturability and design for assembly including experience taking products from prototype design to production 

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing materials, GD&T, and tolerance/stack-up analysis 

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing processes and machines including mills, lathes, welding, sheet-metal bending, lifting/rigging, assembly, inspection, etc. 

• Experience with custom machine design: motors, actuators, linear rails/actuators, pneumatics, bearings, etc.
