jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 Job Description: Senior Manufacturing Engineer, MRO, Turbine Engines

 JOB DESCRIPTION :

 Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 SUMMARY - ABOUT THE TEAM / JOB 
Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer to join our team. The Propulsion Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for the Core Technologies Platform. This responsibility includes everything in the manufacturing value-chain, including, but not limited to, Design for Manufacturability work, tool design & selection, process creation & optimization, vendor sourcing & interaction, quality planning, and work documentation associated with the hardware that the Manufacturing Engineer owns.

The right person for this role can demonstrate past holistic ownership on solving a technical challenge with a creative, physical, solution that they either personally manufacturing or oversaw manufacturing on, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

• Own the disposition and rework of engines that fail internal acceptance test or are returned by customers, addressing both hardware failures and upgrades to the latest configuration for the entire program.

• Diagnose engine-level issues by analyzing test data, inspecting hardware, and driving each failure to its true root cause.

• Author clear, complete rework instructions and partner closely with production to communicate tasks, priorities, and expectations.

• Manage configuration across the EBOM and MBOM to keep every engine traceable to its correct build state.

• Lead teardown and inspection of returned engines, documenting findings and determining whether components are serviceable, repairable, or scrap.

• Define and manage upgrade paths that bring legacy-configuration engines to the current standard, including the required rework steps and parts.

• Feed failure findings back to design, quality, and reliability engineering so recurring issues are corrected at the source.

• Estimate rework scope, cost, and turnaround time, and coordinate with planning and supply chain to signal hardware demand.

• Verify that every reworked engine meets requirements and passes acceptance testing before it ships to the customer.

• Maintain accurate as-built records so each engine's final configuration is fully documented after rework.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field; Master's degree preferred.

• 5+ years of progressive experience in turbomachinery component manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or high-performance industrial gas turbine industries.

• Experience with CAD/CAM software, preferably NX or similar.

• Familiarity with CNC machining, additive manufacturing, and other advanced manufacturing technologies.

• Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

• Strong communication and teamwork skills.

• Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (No minimum requirements, maximum ~5-6 bullet points) 

• Experience integrating automation, robotics, or advanced metrology systems (e.g., CMM, optical scanning) into manufacturing workflows.

• Owned end-to-end equipment development and implementation

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
At ABB , we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

 This position reports to: 
Production Engineering Manager 
 __
 ABB’s Drives factory in Jüri, Estonia, was established in 2005 and is part of ABB’s global Motion business. The factory is one of ABB’s major production sites for low-voltage drives (frequency converters), power inverters and converters. 

 Our products are used across industries, including manufacturing and marine applications, to control electric motors, improve process efficiency and reduce energy consumption by up to 50%. Most of the drives produced in Jüri are exported to global markets.   

 Your role and responsibilities   

 As a Manufacturing Engineer, you will oversee manufacturing processes from process design and industrialization through production ramp-up and ongoing improvement. You will work hands-on with production teams, lead improvement projects and use your engineering expertise to improve productivity, quality, cost and overall manufacturing performance.   

 Working model: onsite #LIonsite  

 • Oversee the development and industrialization of manufacturing processes by defining process sequences, production methods, cycle times, equipment needs, and materials to meet production, quality, cost, and investment goals   
 • Drive the ramp-up of new production lines and products, supporting start-up activities, troubleshooting and implementation of action plans together with Production, Maintenance and other relevant stakeholders   
 • Design, develop and optimise production processes, tooling and fixtures, using Design for Manufacture principles and advanced SolidWorks CAD/CAM skills   
 • Manage continuous improvement initiatives using Lean and Six Sigma methodologies, analysing KPIs, identifying improvement opportunities and delivering projects focused on productivity, quality, cost and waste reduction   
 • Own and continuously improve manufacturing and quality documentation, including process flow charts, FMEA, quality control plans and checklists, while ensuring compliance with defined standards and requirements   
 • Collaborate with internal experts, suppliers and ABB teams across different locations to solve complex manufacturing and quality issues, evaluate new technologies and implement scalable best practices

 Qualification for the role 

 • 5+ years of hands-on experience in a manufacturing environment, with deep experience in engineering and manufacturing processes   
 • B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering or a related technical field.   
 • Strong knowledge of Design for Manufacture, Design for Assembly (DFA) and Design for Quality (DFQ) principles   
 • Deep understanding of Continuous Improvement, Lean Manufacturing, and Six Sigma tools, with practical experience using these methods   
 • Advanced Computer-Aided Design (CAD) skills, preferably SolidWorks CAD/CAM, with experience designing tooling and fixtures   
 • Ability to assess and enhance manufacturing KPIs, determine root causes, and guide improvement efforts from initial concept through full implementation   
 • Strong problem-solving and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work independently, take ownership and drive projects in a hands-on manufacturing environment.   
 • Good command of English and Russian   

 More about us 

 We care. Аbout your health, well-being, and work-life balance. That’s why we offer private health insurance, sports compensation, and other perks to help you feel your best.
 We grow together. You’ll be part of a supportive international team where collaboration is real, not just a buzzword.
 We stay curious. Learning never stops here. From hands-on experience to development programs - you’ll have space to explore, learn, and try new things.
 We value your impact. Your work matters. We offer an annual bonus and celebrate the wins: big or small.
 We keep it modern. With flexible working and smart tools, we make sure your everyday work experience is smooth and up to date.

 For more information, please contact Talent Partner Elena, +372 5680 1416

 We look forward to receiving your application (documents submitted in English are appreciated). 

 Building a cleaner, smarter future takes all kinds of minds: the curious, the courageous, and the creative. That's why we welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences.

 Ready to make an impact? 

 Apply today or visit https://www.abb.com to learn more about the impact of our solutions across the globe.

 ABOUT THE JOB 

 Anduril is seeking a Mechanical Design Engineer to join the Maneuver Dominance team in our Costa Mesa office. The Maneuver Dominance (MD) Team at Anduril develops aerial robotic systems designed to operate in large coordinated teams in concert with ground maneuver forces.

Here you will work on core product development for unmanned rotorcraft and complex systems, including but not limited to design and development of a novel payload carriage and release system, analysis and testing of the system and it’s tooling design. The ideal candidate would be practical, hands-on and a self starter with high growth potential.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Own and drive the physical design of the payload carriage and release for a novel aircraft type.

• Participate in technical efforts to define requirements, propose possible solutions, and establish a methodology for evaluating and verifying mechanical systems. This will involve close collaboration with partner organizations, 

• Work in close partnership with other disciplines internal to Anduril to ensure the electrical, actuation, and mechanical systems collectively form a reliable, flexible, cost-effective system.

• Participate in design reviews, conduct analysis, build prototypes and implement hardware test plans.

• Actively contribute to the enhancement of team tools, templates, processes, and standards.

• Cultivate a vibrant, positive, dedicated and educational collaborative work environment.

• Travel to test sites and vendors to support critical hardware demonstrations and development test activities as needed.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• BEng, BSc, MEng, MSc or higher in mechanical or aerospace engineering, or equivalent work experience.

• 5+ years in a technical engineering role in a professional aerospace setting, with demonstrated track record of technical excellence, design creativity, collaboration and consensus building, and successful product delivery.

• Experience in NX/Teamcenter and proficiency in CAD software with specific emphasis on rapid concepting and iteration of novel designs.

• Ability to demonstrate technical knowledge in core engineering principles, including fundamental mechanics of composite and metallic materials, design, analysis, testing, and fabrication.

• Understanding of load paths, design practices, and hand calculations to design robust structurally efficient assemblies.

• An excellent communicator, experienced in report writing and the development and delivery of presentations across a range of settings.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.K. security clearance.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience with design and development of payload carriage and release systems.

• Experience in systems integration during airframe assembly, particularly focusing on mechanical systems.

• Demonstrated passion for aviation, aerospace, and/or unmanned systems.

jobs.title: Senior Equipment & Tool Engineer
jobs.desc:
Senior Equipment & Tool Engineer 

 Company: 
The Boeing Company 

 Boeing Defense, Space & Security (BDS) is seeking a Senior Equipment & Tool Engineer to join the Test Equipment Engineering team in Heath, OH.

 The Senior Equipment & Tool Engineer (Mid-Level) is responsible for analyzing, procuring, and managing spare parts and electronic components for all test stations. This role coordinates cross‑functional engineering efforts and vendor activities to support test station readiness, drives obsolescence mitigation and design updates, and leads customer presentations and approvals through a formal change working group.

 Position Responsibilities: 
 • Analyze spare parts and electronic component requirements for all test stations; maintain accurate spare parts lists and forecasts
• Work with internal functions (test engineering, design, manufacturing, procurement, quality, and logistics) to define, prioritize, and obtain required parts
• Source and manage relationships with outside vendors and distributors for components and assemblies; ensure delivery schedules and quality requirements are met
• Monitor component lifecycle and lead obsolescence risk assessments; identify alternatives, design changes, or requalification needs to mitigate obsolescence impacts
• Coordinate design updates and suggestions between engineers for hardware, firmware, and test station software; capture engineering change requests (ECRs) and drive engineering change notices (ECNs)
• Maintain and update BOMs, CAD/PLM records, and spare parts databases to reflect current configurations and approved changes
• Prepare and present proposed design changes, obsolescence plans, and spare parts strategies to customers and stakeholders; lead discussions with customer representatives
• Facilitate customer approvals through the established change working group or configuration control board; document approvals and disposition actions
• Support test station sustainment activities, troubleshoot part failures, and recommend corrective actions or upgrades
• Ensure compliance with company policies and relevant quality standards (e.g., AS9100), export control, and procurement procedures
• Track metrics for spare parts availability, lead times, cost, and obsolescence risk; report status to management and stakeholders
• Participate in continuous improvement activities to optimize spare parts management, reduce costs, and improve test station uptime

 Basic Qualifications (Required Skills and Experience): 
 • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering Technology, Mechanical Engineering, or related technical discipline
• 5+ years of experience in test equipment support, spare parts management, procurement coordination, or obsolescence management in an aerospace, defense, or electronics environment
• Practical knowledge of electronic components, assemblies, and test station hardware
• Experience with engineering change processes (ECR/ECN), BOM/PLM systems, and ERP/MRP tools

 Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills and Experience): 
 • Strong vendor management and procurement coordination experience
• Demonstrated ability to present technical information to customers and lead cross‑functional change approval processes
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including technical documentation and presentation skills
• Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders
• Familiarity with industry standards and practices for obsolescence management
• Experience with contract/customer-facing change boards or working groups
• Certifications such as IPC, ASQ, Six Sigma, or relevant procurement/supply chain certifications

 Conflict of Interest: 
 Successful candidates for this job must satisfy the Company’s Conflict of Interest (COI) assessment process.

 Relocation: 
 Relocation assistance is not a negotiable benefit for this position. Candidates must live in the immediate area or relocate at their own expense.

 Drug Free Workplace: 
 Boeing is a Drug Free Workplace (DFW) where post offer applicants and employees are subject to testing for marijuana, cocaine, opioids, amphetamines, PCP, and alcohol when criteria is met as outlined in our policies.

 The Boeing 401(k) helps you save for your future, with contributions from Boeing that can help you grow your retirement savings. Our best-in-class retirement benefit features:
 • Best in class 401(k) plan: we'll match your contributions dollar for dollar, up to 10% of eligible pay with Immediate 100% vesting 
• Student Loan Match : The Boeing 401(k) Student Loan Match allows eligible enrolled U.S. employees to have their qualified student loan debt payments counted, along with any match-eligible contributions they make, for purposes of determining the Company Match to employees' Boeing 401(k) accounts. 

 Pay & Benefits: 
 At Boeing, we strive to deliver a Total Rewards package that will attract, engage and retain the top talent. Elements of the Total Rewards package include competitive base pay and variable compensation opportunities.

 The Boeing Company also provides eligible employees with an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs, generally including health insurance, flexible spending accounts, health savings accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and a number of programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work.

 The specific programs and options available to any given employee may vary depending on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

 Pay is based upon candidate experience and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

 $126,650-$171,350a

Not Applicable

Bachelor's Degree or Equivalent

jobs.desc:
Job Description Summary 

 Job Description 
 Working at our Clearwater Location 
 Clearwater is a provider of engineering, circuit card assembly, OEM Avionics, and MRO services to commercial and military customers. Products and technologies here are diverse and highly sophisticated. Your work will contribute to systems that manage the performance of Boeing 737 and 787 aircraft as well as F-18s, F-35s, Harriers, and Apaches. Not only will you work in a facility that has been awarded OSHAS’s highest safety rating, but you’ll be part of a diverse team of employees working together to impact the future of flight for generations.

 Role Overview 
 The Lead Manufacturing Engineer (2nd shift) will be responsible for the development and implementation of manufacturing processes, ensuring they meet our stringent safety, quality, delivery, and cost objectives. This role requires a strong background in manufacturing engineering, project management, and a deep understanding of Lean manufacturing principles.

 Roles and Responsibilities 
 • Utilize your experience or expertise to solve problems, develop and execute objectives for self and others, and have the ability to effect short-term and some long-term business goals
• Develop and maintain manufacturing work instructions and related documentation
• Design and build / procure necessary fixtures and tooling to manufacture electronic assemblies and products
• Support assembly equipment upgrades from purchase through installation
• Conduct cost / benefit analysis for changes to manufacturing processes and / or equipment
• Assist Production Supervisors and production employees in resolving manufacturing process problems through a drive to root cause and permanent corrective action
• Support EHS projects in cell
• Drive Process Improvement / Cycle Reduction initiatives and drive productivity improvements via process changes or improvements
• Support the quality function through integration of ISO / QC documentation and manufacturing work instructions
• Lead high impact process and quality improvement projects yielding significant reduction in defects and increased productivity in the Cell
• Attend weekly cross-functional quality sessions and track/drive root cause analysis and corrective actions for Cell issues
• Lead New Technology Initiatives (NTI) and share best practices with other locations
• Utilize lean-manufacturing principles and participate in action workouts to improve process capability, reduce overall costs and increase capacity defects and increased productivity in the Cell

 Required Qualifications 
 • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university (or a High School diploma / GED with at least 7 years of experience in Manufacturing / Production)
• Minimum of 3 years of experience in electronics assembly environments
• This position requires U.S. citizenship status

 Preferred Qualifications 
 • Experience in running, supporting, troubleshooting, fixing, and resolving line issues with some of the following Circuit Card Assembly Cells: SMT Prep, Mag-Load, Fuji SMT, SPI, Reflow Ovens, Through Hole, Hand Assembly, Selective Solder, Wave Solder, Bonding, Conformal Coating, DePanel, Final Assembly, and Box load
• Experience in supporting and programming some of the following CCA assembly equipment: Glue Machine, Laser Etcher, SPI, Fuji AIMEX III SMT, AOI, Xray, AXI, Press Fit, Trace Cut, Aqueous Wash, Conformal Coating, PVA, Selective Solder, Wave Solder, and BGA Rework
• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Manufacturing, or Industrial Engineering
• Ability to read engineering drawings and specifications
• Strong mechanical design ability
• Ability to manage priorities and achieve results
• Prior exposure to and knowledge of Lean Manufacturing
• Strong Project Management skills
• Strong manufacturing process knowledge
• Strong oral and written communication skills
• Strong interpersonal and leadership skills

 This role requires access to U.S. export-controlled information. Therefore, employment will be contingent upon the ability to prove that you meet the status of a U.S. Person as one of the following: U.S. lawful permanent resident, U.S. Citizen, have been granted asylee or refugee status (i.e., a protected individual under the Immigration and Naturalization Act, 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)). 

 Additional Information 
 GE Aerospace offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE Aerospace is an  Equal Opportunity Employer . jobs.title: Lead Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
Job Description Summary 
The Lead Manufacturing Engineer – Development Readiness, Manufacturing Readiness leads manufacturing readiness, process maturation, and launch execution for Next Gen Product and process technologies. This role partners with design engineering, quality, supply chain, and operations to ensure producible designs, mature manufacturing methods, and robust production readiness plans that support Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost objectives.
The role combines MRL leadership, advanced process development, NPI execution, and operational integration to bridge the gap between early technology development and full-rate production. The leader establishes operating mechanisms, readiness reviews, dashboards, and action plans that connect technology maturation and manufacturing risk reduction to program execution. 

 Job Description 
 • Roles and Responsibilities 
• Own and lead MRL execution for assigned programs, including assessments, gap closure plans, evidence-based gate reviews, and readiness reporting
• Translate technology roadmaps and product requirements into executable manufacturing development and production readiness plans
• Partner with design engineering to improve producibility early in the design cycle by incorporating manufacturing capability, process constraints, and risk mitigation
• Develop and mature manufacturing processes for advanced or special process applications, including production methods, tooling concepts, fixtures, and shop implementation strategies
• Lead cross-functional tollgates, tier reviews, CDRL reviews and readiness reviews across engineering, quality, supply chain, and operations
• Build and maintain dashboards, visual management tools, and action trackers to monitor MRL maturity, launch risk, deployment progress, and SQDC performance
• Support APQP, PFMEA, control plans, and structured problem - solving to reduce manufacturing risk and stabilize execution
• Work with production teams to ensure processes are ready for rate, yield, quality, and delivery performance

jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Factory Test team designs, builds, and operates the infrastructure needed to test nearly every part of Terran R right here at our headquarters in Long Beach, CA. This centralized approach provides engineers and technicians with exposure to the entire product lifecycle across a wide range of part sizes and complexities. The scope and scale are significant, with test stands capable of handling millions of pounds of force. Team members lead multiple projects in parallel, avoiding silos and gaining broad technical experience without needing a background in aerospace. With high-impact campaigns ahead, including thrust structure and stage 2 testing, now is the time to join. You won’t just execute, but you’ll help shape and scale the test infrastructure required to meet the demands of a rapidly growing launch program. 

 About the Role: 

• Develop detailed process plans, work instructions, and work orders for the integration and test of flight hardware, including propulsion components, structural assemblies, fluid systems, and instrumentation. 

• Collaborate with design and test engineers to provide design for testability feedback, ensuring hardware is robust and efficient in the test environment. 

• Support test technicians and test specialists on the floor by troubleshooting issues, resolving non-conformances, and implementing corrective actions in real time. 

• Coordinate with quality teams to ensure timely procurement and inspection of critical test components and verify all required calibrated equipment is in-date, documented on the work order, and available at time of use. 

• Conduct Test Readiness Reviews (TRRs) to ensure all hardware is test-ready and risks are mitigated prior to test execution. 

• Analyze process performance, test timelines, and drive continuous improvement across test campaigns. 

• Maintain capacity and demand plans for upcoming test articles and support equipment. 

 About You: 

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. 

• 4+ years of experience in manufacturing, test engineering, or process development for aerospace hardware. 

• Hands-on experience supporting hardware builds in development and test environments. 

• Familiarity with pressure systems, instrumentation, and fluid system assembly. 

• Experience with manufacturing documentation including work instructions, test plans. 

• Comfortable working in fast-paced, hands-on environments with shifting priorities. 

 Nice to Haves But Not Required: 

• Experience supporting ATP, development, or qualification test campaigns. 

• Familiarity with high-pressure fluid systems, cryogenic hardware, or propulsion test equipment. 

• Experience with CAD tools (e.g., NX, SolidWorks) and fluid schematics for system layout and planning. 

• Familiarity with PLM and ERP systems for tracking hardware and managing workflow. 

• Understanding of AS9100 or ISO9001 quality management systems.

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.  NEUTRON 

 Neutron is a medium lift launch vehicle capable of delivering the mega constellations of tomorrow, high assurance payloads, and human spaceflight. As a highly reusable launch platform, Neutron will deliver a highly cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab’s proven execution history with the Electron program. If you’re interested in joining a high performing team, pushing the boundaries with a clean sheet development of re-usable liquid launch vehicle, this is your opportunity!

 MANUFACTURING ENGINEER II 

 T he Neutron Manufacturing Engineer is responsible for integration, test and launch of the Neutron launch vehicle. This position will work closely with the Neutron Manufacturing Engineer and other key team members. Job scope will include developing processes, working in a team environment, identifying and design build of necessary equipment for receipt and final integration, and launch of the Neutron Launch Vehicle.

 WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO: 

• Develop con-ops, design and drive build of associated ground support tooling and processes for handling components and integrated stages of the Neutron Launch Vehicle.

• Develop and execute procedures for the integration of Neutron Launch Vehicle flight hardware and ground support equipment.

• Support Neutron Integration Manager in developing and enabling day-to-day execution of the 1 st and 2 nd stage vehicle integration, propellant system, avionics, and AFTS. Including:

• Development and design high-level vehicle maintenance architecture including build flow and test operations for maximum efficiency.

• Development and execute vehicle system level checkouts for initial and flown launch vehicle and components.

• Contribute, develop, and own work procedures and documentation of non-conformances into actionable items and system improvements.

• Maintain integrated planning documents that are inclusive of Launch Vehicle configurations and work scope.

• Design and develop tools and hardware to enable vehicle processing and ensure required testing abilities.

• Develop, build, and maintain Neutron processing facilities.

• Closely collaborate with management staff and peers from other departments and highly skilled technicians on daily routine

• Manage and track multiple priorities while maintaining a focus towards common project goals.

 YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A MANUFACTURING ENGINEER II 

• Bachelor of Science degree in aerospace, mechanical, or manufacturing engineering required.

• 2+ years of experience in building and testing of hardware associated to a launch vehicle and its environments.

• Demonstrated proficiency in authoring comprehensive work instructions and procedures for assembly, test, and launch.

• Proven ability to interface with multidisciplinary functions of mechanical, electrical, and fluid systems.

 THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE: 

• Master of Science degree in aerospace, mechanical, or manufacturing or equivalent

• Experience and demonstrated proficiency in developing and utilizing comprehensive work instructions and test procedures.

• Experience working directly with launch vehicle and/or launch vehicle hardware and subsystems including, avionics, high pressure gas, structures, electrical, and mechanical.

• Experience working on build, test of complex assemblies at the system and sub-system level.

• Demonstrated experience of Project Management principles in previous job experience(s).

 This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas. 

 The expected salary range for the position is displayed in accordance with the state of Virginia’s pay transparency requirements. Final agreed upon compensation is based upon individual qualifications and experience. 

 Base salary is only one part of Rocket Lab’s compensation package for this role. You may be eligible for company stock, or cash incentives, and can purchase discounted stock through Rocket Lab’s Employee Stock Purchase Program. Employee benefits also include medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage; 401(k) retirement plan options; paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave; paid parental leave; and other discounts and perks.

We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. jobs.title: Staff DFx Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology.  ABOUT THE TEAM 

Anduril’s Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a Staff DFx Manufacturing Engineer to drive design-for-manufacturability, assembly, and testability across our avionics, electronics, and harnessing subsystems. This role spans our full portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions — ensuring that electronics hardware is designed to be produced at scale from the earliest stages of development.

As a Staff-level individual contributor, you will be the technical authority on DFx for electronics and avionics across AD&S. You will embed with design engineering teams during concept and detailed design, lead structured DFx reviews, and translate manufacturing constraints into actionable design guidance. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily alongside supply chain, design engineering, quality, and operations teams to ensure producibility is built into every decision, from component selection through final acceptance. Your work directly shapes whether our products can be built reliably, affordably, and at the rate our programs demand.

You will also mentor manufacturing engineers across programs and build the DFx methodology and toolset that scales with the organization. 

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

• Own and drive the DFx process for avionics, electronics, and harnessing subsystems across AD&S programs, from concept through rate production.

• Lead structured DFM/DFA/DFT reviews at key design milestones, applying a rigorous scoring methodology to identify producibility risks and drive design changes before they become production problems.

• Embed with electrical and avionics design engineering teams to provide real-time manufacturing feedback on PCBA layout, component selection, connector and harnessing architecture, and test access.

• Work cross-functionally with supply chain, quality, operations, and design engineering on a daily basis — this role is the connective tissue between what gets designed and what gets built.

• Develop and maintain DFx standards, guidelines, and scorecards specific to electronics manufacturing processes including SMT, wave/selective solder, conformal coating, potting, wire harness fabrication, and box-build assembly.

• Analyze designs across five key lenses — manufacturability/assembly, quality, adherence to

• specification, process capability, and technology maturity — to produce quantified risk assessments that inform engineering and program decisions.

• Champion testability early in the design cycle: define test point access, boundary scan requirements, functional test strategies, and fixtures needed for production-rate acceptance testing.

• Partner with quality engineering to ensure DFx findings flow into inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and process control strategies.

• Collaborate with supply chain and sourcing teams to assess supplier manufacturing capability, support make-vs-buy decisions, and ensure external production meets DFx requirements.

• Close the loop between production floor feedback and upstream design improvements by working directly with operations and production engineering teams.

• Build and evolve the DFx toolkit — templates, scoring rubrics, lessons-learned databases, and training materials — so that DFx knowledge scales beyond any single person.

• Mentor and develop junior and mid-level manufacturing engineers on DFx principles and review techniques.

• Travel to production sites, suppliers, and partner facilities as needed (<10%).

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.

• 12+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, process engineering, or producibility engineering with a significant focus on electronics, avionics, or electromechanical assemblies. A

• Master’s Degree can replace 2 years of work experience.

• Deep working knowledge of electronics manufacturing processes: SMT placement and reflow, wave and selective soldering, conformal coating, potting and encapsulation, cable and harness fabrication, and electromechanical box-build.

• Demonstrated experience leading DFM/DFA/DFT reviews and translating findings into measurable design improvements.

• Proven ability to work cross-functionally across design engineering, supply chain, quality, and operations — and to be effective without positional authority.

• Ability to read and critically evaluate electrical schematics, PCB layouts, harness drawings, and mechanical packaging for producibility.

• Strong command of IPC standards (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, IPC-620, IPC-6012) and their application to design and process decisions.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present DFx findings to engineering leadership and drive alignment on design changes.

• Comfortable working across multiple programs simultaneously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

• Personal experience physically building or reworking electronic assemblies (soldering, harness build, test, debug). Hands-on credibility matters.

 About You:

 Montreal, Canada 

 Une opportunité intéressante pour un Ingénieur Manufacturier - Réparation de composants pour l'aviation civile s'est présentée dans nos installations de Montréal. Dans ce rôle, vous serez responsable de fournir un soutien technique aux opérations et exécuter des activités d'ingénierie de fabrication pour développer, maintenir et améliorer continuellement les processus de fabrication et/ou les méthodes de fabrication, qui sont capables de répondre et de continuer à répondre aux exigences commerciales et des clients en matière de sécurité, de qualité, de coût, de taux de livraison et les délais (SQCD).

 Innover et propulser le monde 
 Chez Rolls-Royce, nous sommes les pionniers de la puissance qui compte pour nos clients, pour la société et pour la planète.

 Nous fournissons les meilleurs moteurs à réaction au monde. Grâce à une innovation intelligente et à une collaboration active, nous plaçons nos clients à l'avant-garde de l'industrie aéronautique - et nous les y maintenons. Notre portefeuille de produits équipe plus de 35 types d'avions commerciaux et compte plus de 13 000 moteurs en service dans le monde ; nous faisons voler le monde.

 Partenaire de confiance au Canada 
 Depuis plus de 75 ans, Rolls-Royce a solidement établi sa présence au Canada. Nous sommes reconnus comme le centre d'excellence mondial en MRO (Maintenance, Réparation, Révision) des moteurs d'avions d'affaires Rolls-Royce, ayant entretenu plus de 6 300 moteurs qui volent dans le monde entier dans le secteur des jets d'affaires et privés. Nous recherchons des personnes talentueuses pour nous rejoindre.

 À notre usine de Lachine, nous comptons actuellement 600 employés. Nous recherchons des personnes techniques compétentes et motivées pour rejoindre notre équipe soudée et nous aider à réaliser notre ambitieux plan de croissance. Ce plan est crucial pour nous permettre de rester à l'avant-garde des besoins de nos clients et d'innover continuellement.

 Ce que vous obtiendrez 
 • Salaire très compétitif

• L'un des régimes de retraite à cotisation définies les plus compétitifs

• Régime d'assurance maladie et dentaire collectif flexible

• Nombre généreux de jours personnels par an

• Club social

• Service de cafétéria

 Principales responsabilités :

 • Sécurité des produits - Assurez-vous que les processus de fabrication sont capables d'atteindre et de maintenir l'intention de conception, et que les processus sont suivis afin que nos produits et ceux de nos fournisseurs soient conformes à leurs spécifications. Soulever, enquêter et résoudre rigoureusement les problèmes liés à la sécurité.

 • Qualité - Conduire une culture du zéro défaut au sein de l'organisation. Fonctionne avec toutes les fonctions pour réduire les risques et piloter le produit du premier coup. Assurer la conformité à toutes les politiques et normes pertinentes de l'entreprise, législatives et techniques, y compris les exigences RRMS, sabre et de contrôle des exportations et de propriété intellectuelle.

 • Autorité technique - Assurer l'application des contrôles du processus de fabrication dans son domaine de responsabilité, avec autorisation sous réserve de délégation appropriée. Agir en tant que signataire MEA, le cas échéant.

 • Planification - Planifiez et gérez les activités, y compris le calendrier, les ressources et les coûts, en obtenant l'achat et en communiquant l'état actuel aux parties prenantes concernées. Veiller à ce que les problèmes et les risques soient résolus pour respecter les délais du projet.

 • Développer la capacité - Développer, mettre en œuvre, valider, maintenir et améliorer en permanence les processus de fabrication, les systèmes numériques et/ou les méthodes de fabrication qui sont capables de répondre et de continuer à répondre aux exigences de sécurité, de qualité, de coût, de taux de livraison et de délai. Capturez, analysez et utilisez des données pour démontrer et améliorer la capacité actuelle et future des processus de fabrication.

 • IT Normes minimales - En collaboration avec la fonction d'ingénierie de fabrication et les propriétaires de processus de fabrication, dirigez les processus de fabrication vers les meilleures pratiques cohérentes identifiées.

 • Collaboration et partage des connaissances - Travailler avec des équipes d'interface et des experts locaux pour s'assurer que les aspects techniques des processus de fabrication et des systèmes numériques sont compris et pris en compte selon les besoins. Capturez et utilisez les leçons apprises. Identifier, documenter et partager les meilleures pratiques, notamment en participant aux communautés de pratique pertinentes.

jobs.desc:
About Lucid 

 At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience. 

 We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility. 

 About the Team

 The General Assembly Advanced Manufacturing Engineering team enables Lucid to launch safe, efficient, production-ready assembly processes at scale. The team partners across Product Design, Quality, Operations, Maintenance, Facilities, Supply Chain, and external suppliers to translate vehicle requirements into capable manufacturing equipment and tooling. This group is unique in its end-to-end ownership of equipment strategy, supplier execution, validation, installation, commissioning, and operational handoff, giving team members direct visibility into how engineering decisions affect quality, throughput, safety, and launch readiness.

 About the Role

 The Manufacturing Engineer is an individual contributor role within General Assembly Advanced Manufacturing Engineering and reports to a Manufacturing Engineering leader. This role exists to support Lucid’s growth by strengthening equipment procurement, integration, validation, and launch readiness for General Assembly programs. In the first 12 months, this person will own assigned equipment and tooling projects from scope development through validated production handoff, with success measured by safe installation, capable processes, clear documentation, on-time issue closure, and readiness for Operations ownership.  What You Own

• Equipment Strategy: Define equipment and tooling scopes, technical specifications, and RFQ packages that align safety, quality, cycle time, throughput, maintainability, timing, and cost requirements before supplier award.

• Supplier Alignment: Evaluate supplier proposals, lead technical clarification, and partner with Purchasing to support supplier selection, purchase-order execution, commercial alignment, and on-time delivery.

• Project Execution: Lead assigned equipment projects from design approval through build, Factory Acceptance Testing, shipment, installation, commissioning, ramp-up, and final acceptance.

• Launch Readiness: Develop and manage project schedules, budgets, risk registers, open-issue lists, recovery plans, and escalation paths to keep equipment launches on track.

• Cross-Functional Integration: Coordinate Product Design, Quality, Operations, Maintenance, Facilities, Supply Chain, and supplier partners to resolve technical and launch issues with clear ownership and timely decisions.

• Process Validation: Define and confirm acceptance criteria for safety, ergonomics, quality, cycle time, throughput, maintainability, and specification compliance before handoff to Operations.

• Operational Handoff: Deliver validated equipment, process documentation, training inputs, spare-parts requirements, open-item closure plans, and lessons learned that improve future launch execution.

 What You Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 6 years of manufacturing engineering experience in assembly operations, equipment integration, production launch, or a related manufacturing environment.

• Working knowledge of assembly processes, tooling, automation, equipment integration, and production-launch execution.

• Experience preparing technical documentation or RFQ inputs and supporting design reviews, acceptance testing, installation, commissioning, or operational handoff.

• Ability to read, write, speak, and understand English sufficiently to perform the essential duties of the position, including understanding work instructions, safety procedures, and job-related communications.

 Preferred Qualifications

• Automotive General Assembly, electric vehicle, or new-product-introduction experience.

• Experience with CATIA or similar CAD tools, 3DEXPERIENCE, MS Project, Jira, Smartsheet, or Microsoft Office.

• Experience developing equipment budgets, risk assessments, acceptance criteria, launch-readiness documentation, or handoff packages.

• Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, PFMEA, control plans, GD&T, equipment safety, ergonomics, maintainability, or production quality requirements.

 Physical Requirements

• Standing and Walking: Ability to stand and walk for extended periods in a production environment.

• Manual Dexterity: Frequent use of hands for handling tools, reviewing equipment, and supporting assembly or commissioning activities.

• Lifting and Carrying: Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull items up to 50 lbs. as needed; heavier lifts may require assistance.

• Reaching and Bending: Ability to reach, bend, twist, and squat while supporting equipment installation, validation, and production-floor activities.

• PPE Expectations: Must wear required PPE, which may include safety shoes, gloves, protective sleeves, eye protection, and hearing protection, based on area requ

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. • Collaborate with quality engineering to understand how DFx findings translate into inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and supplier quality requirements.

• Spend time on the production floor and at supplier sites to build firsthand understanding of how electronics and harnesses are manufactured.

• Contribute to the DFx toolkit — templates, scoring rubrics, cost models, lessons-learned databases, and training materials.

• Travel to production sites, contract manufacturers, and supplier facilities (~20%, depending on business needs).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.

• Foundational knowledge of electronics and/or harnessing manufacturing processes: SMT, soldering, conformal coating, wire harness fabrication, or electromechanical assembly.

• Ability to read electrical schematics, PCB layouts, and harness drawings with an eye toward producibility.

• Interest in understanding manufacturing cost drivers and how design decisions impact unit cost.

• Familiarity with IPC standards (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, IPC-620) or a willingness to learn and apply them quickly.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer II, Structures
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the team: 

 The Stage Manufacturing team turns design into reality, owning the build of Terran R’s primary structures. This isn’t about turning the same bolt every day; it’s about building the systems to build the rocket. Engineers and technicians work side by side, with deep collaboration and real-time feedback, to shape how we build better and faster. With a manifest and a launch date, it’s up to the team to deliver on Terran R: solving challenges in real time, optimizing for scale, and constantly improving processes. As the vehicle evolves, so will the factory, with opportunities to apply automation, machine learning, and advanced technologies. What we build here sets the blueprint for the future of scaled launch. 

 About the role: 

• Cover the shop floor for a primary structure assembly work center (or multiple), clearing barriers and keeping production moving 

• Champion process improvements across multiple work centers to improve assembly operations and incorporate feedback and learnings from the first Terran R build 

• Collaborate closely with a diverse team of engineers specializing in design, manufacturing, and reliability, as well as internal production teams and external vendors, leveraging their collective expertise to drive progress 

• Create work instructions, specifications, and best practices across multiple high-fidelity processes. Help standardize processes across the manufacturing team. 

• Provide Design for Manufacturing feedback to structures teams during the development phase and through the first prototype and flight builds 

 About You: 

• Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, aeronautical, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline 

• 2+ years progressive and related experience required 

• Hands on project history of supporting complicated assembly builds and capable of making risk decisions on a regular basis to disposition issues during build and keep production moving 

• Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with engineering and manufacturing groups to understand process constraints and provide design inputs for improved manufacturability 

• Strong engineering fundamentals in statics, mechanics of materials, process improvement/factory design, fastening and joining, machining 

• Knowledge of common drilling and trim ops, other manufacturing processes, tools, inspection methods and GD&T 

• Highly self-motivated and able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment 

 Nice to have: 

• Direct experience with drill, trim and fastening operations for aerospace products 

• New product introduction of an aerospace hardware system into a manufacturing, test, and production system with proven success 

• Experience in managing projects in a fast-paced environment 

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here. 

 Hiring Range:
 $104,000 — $156,000 USD 

 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 

 If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at accommodations@relativityspace.com . 

 Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission - via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee - will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.

jobs.desc:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB 

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

 SPACE SYSTEMS 

 At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

 Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

 HARNESS DESIGN ENGINEER II 

 Based out of Rocket Lab's global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Harness Design Engineer II will primarily work on design of electrical harnesses for our spacecraft, including organizing interfaces, selecting components, specifying split locations and lengths, and generating design documentation to pass to our spacecraft engineering team to allow accurate CAD models to be made. Since this role will have heavy involvement in electronics, you will also get to assist in the execution of electrical engineering activities for our spacecraft and space systems components. This includes assisting our avionics designers with circuit design, analysis, prototyping and testing.

• Harnessing responsibilities:

• Perform or support design tasks such as harness layout, connector and back shell selection, wire selection, and shielding for our spacecraft.

• Generate pinout tables for harness connectors at both ends of the assembly based on spacecraft interconnect diagrams

• Responsible for creating and maintaining BOMs for harnessing in our product lifecycle management (PLM) tool

• Assist in creating documentation for electrical system schematics and harness designs

• Avionics responsibilities:

• Develop test plans and procedures for avionics subsystems and components

• Perform analysis and evaluations to optimize spacecraft avionics circuits for performance, reliability, and manufacturability.

• Participate in internal design and customer facing review meetings as a representative of the avionics electrical engineering team.

• Work in multi-disciplinary teams to assist in design of electronic assemblies for our satellite and spacecraft programs

 QUALIFICATIONS YOU’LL BRING: 

• Bachelor’s degree in aerospace, mechanical, or electrical engineering; or other engineering degree

• 2+ years of electrical engineering or avionics experience

• US citizenship is required, due to program requirements

 THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE: 

• Master’s or PhD in aerospace, mechanical, or electrical engineering; or other engineering degree

• Experience in the aerospace/defense industry

• Experience supporting satellite development programs and satellite operations

• Thorough understanding of the space environment, orbital mechanics, and rigid body dynamics

• Experience with LT Spice, Altium, and/or Siemens software suite (i.e. Teamcenter)

• Experience with requirement management tools such as JAMA

• Experience with testing electrical subsystems and assemblies, thermal vacuum or random vibration, and hardware-in-the loop (HITL) testing

• Proficiency in electronics principles and electrical systems, including power electronics, communication systems (e.g. RS-422, SPI, Ethernet, CAN bus), signal integrity, and grounding

• Proficiency with instrumentation, interfaces, and sensors, including power supplies, oscilloscopes, serial devices, accelerometers, thermocouples, RTDs, and 4-20mA sensors

• Ability to work in a dynamic environment with competing priorities

 This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

 NEUTRON 

 Rocket Lab’s Neutron team is responsible for bringing our new large rocket Neutron and its launch and test sites to life. From designing and testing Neutron’s structures and components, to firing up its new Archimedes engines, to setting up Neutron’s launch pads and test sites across the United States, joining the Neutron team is your opportunity to help launch a new large rocket for the very first time. 

 PROPULSION DESIGN ENGINEER II 

 Based out of Rocket Lab's our headquarters in Long Beach, CA the Propulsion Design Engineer is responsible for the design of engine components (combustion chambers, turbo machinery, engine layout, etc.) for the Archimedes Engine. In this role you’ll have the opportunity to design, analyze and build hardware. jobs.desc:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB 

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

 SPACE SYSTEMS 

 At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

 Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

 HARNESS DESIGN ENGINEER II 

 Based out of Rocket Lab's global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Harness Design Engineer II will primarily work on design of electrical harnesses for our spacecraft, including organizing interfaces, selecting components, specifying split locations and lengths, and generating design documentation to pass to our spacecraft engineering team to allow accurate CAD models to be made. Since this role will have heavy involvement in electronics, you will also get to assist in the execution of electrical engineering activities for our spacecraft and space systems components. This includes assisting our avionics designers with circuit design, analysis, prototyping and testing.

 WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO: 

• Harnessing responsibilities:

• Perform or support design tasks such as harness layout, connector and back shell selection, wire selection, and shielding for our spacecraft.

• Generate pinout tables for harness connectors at both ends of the assembly based on spacecraft interconnect diagrams

• Responsible for creating and maintaining BOMs for harnessing in our product lifecycle management (PLM) tool

• Assist in creating documentation for electrical system schematics and harness designs

• Avionics responsibilities:

• Develop test plans and procedures for avionics subsystems and components

• Perform analysis and evaluations to optimize spacecraft avionics circuits for performance, reliability, and manufacturability.

• Participate in internal design and customer facing review meetings as a representative of the avionics electrical engineering team.

• Work in multi-disciplinary teams to assist in design of electronic assemblies for our satellite and spacecraft programs

 QUALIFICATIONS YOU’LL BRING AS HARNESS DESIGN ENGINEER II: 

• Bachelor’s degree in aerospace, mechanical, or electrical engineering; or other engineering degree

• 2+ years of electrical engineering or avionics experience

• U.S citizenship required, due to program requirements

 THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE: 

• Master’s or PhD in aerospace, mechanical, or electrical engineering; or other engineering degree

• Experience in the aerospace/defense industry

• Experience supporting satellite development programs and satellite operations

• Thorough understanding of the space environment, orbital mechanics, and rigid body dynamics

• Experience with LT Spice, Altium, and/or Siemens software suite (i.e. Teamcenter)

• Experience with requirement management tools such as JAMA

• Experience with testing electrical subsystems and assemblies, thermal vacuum or random vibration, and hardware-in-the loop (HITL) testing

• Proficiency in electronics principles and electrical systems, including power electronics, communication systems (e.g. RS-422, SPI, Ethernet, CAN bus), signal integrity, and grounding

• Proficiency with instrumentation, interfaces, and sensors, including power supplies, oscilloscopes, serial devices, accelerometers, thermocouples, RTDs, and 4-20mA sensors

• Ability to work in a dynamic environment with competing priorities

 This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

 You'll have the opportunity to work on cutting-edge applications, develop breakthrough technologies, and deliver innovative solutions to some of the world’s leading automotive brands. See your work come to life on the road—helping make mobility safer, greener, and more connected. Ready to shape the future of mobility with us?

 YOUR ROLE 
 As the Lean Manufacturing Engineer you will be responsible for:

 - Production Launch Planning: Develop launch plans, milestones, and SOP readiness activities. 
 - Process Development: Define and validate manufacturing processes, work instructions, and assembly sequences. 
 - Equipment and Tooling Readiness: Ensure equipment, fixtures, and tooling are installed, commissioned, and capable. 
 - Process Validation: Support prototype, pilot, and pre-production builds and verify cycle times. 
 - Quality Assurance During Launch: Support PFMEA, Control Plans, defect reduction, and corrective actions. 
 - Capacity and Productivity Management: Confirm production rates, line balancing, and resource utilization. 
 - Cross Functional Coordination: Work with Engineering, Quality, Production, Maintenance, Logistics, and Suppliers. 
 - Risk Management: Identify launch risks, maintain action plans, and escalate critical issues. 
 - Launch Issue Management: Lead tracking and closure of open issues affecting successful product launch. 
 - Customer Focus: Ensure customer requirements are met and launch objectives support customer satisfaction. 

 RESPONSABILITIES 
 • Lead new product launch activities from planning through production stabilization. 

 • Develop, validate, and continuously improve manufacturing processes, work instructions, and assembly methods. 

 • Coordinate equipment, tooling, quality, production, maintenance, logistics, and supplier readiness to ensure successful product launches. 

 • Manage PFMEA, Control Plans, process documentation, and launch performance metrics. 

 • Identify and mitigate launch risks, drive issue resolution, and ensure customer requirements are achieved. 

 • Monitor post-launch performance and support transition to normal production operations. 

• High energy, results-oriented, 5+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, product launches, process development, and cross-functional project coordination within a high-volume manufacturing environment. 

 REQUIRED SKILLS 

 • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field. 

 • 5+ years of experience in Manufacturing Engineering, Launch Engineering, or Process Engineering.  

 • Experience with PFMEA, Control Plans, Process Flow Diagrams, and manufacturing documentation.  

 • Strong project management and problem-solving skills. 

 • Experience supporting new product launches and process validation activities. 

 • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications. 

 • English 80%  

 Nice to Have (Preferred Qualifications)  
 • Experience in automotive manufacturing environments.  

 • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies. 

 • APQP and PPAP experience. 

 • Familiarity with OEE, FPY, cycle time analysis, and capacity planning. 

 • Experience working with automated assembly equipment and production systems.  

 • Green Belt or equivalent continuous improvement certification .  

 WHY JOIN US? 

 • You can grow at Aptiv. Aptiv provides an inclusive work environment where all individuals can grow and develop, regardless of gender, ethnicity or beliefs.
• You can have an impact . Safety is a core Aptiv value; we want a safer world for us and our children, one with: Zero fatalities, Zero injuries, Zero accidents.
• You have support . We ensure you have the resources and support you need to take care of your family and your physical and mental health with a competitive health insurance package.

 Schaeffler Group USA Inc.  

 Jason Gould

At ABB , we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

Production Development Specialist 
 __

Each day, you will ensure appropriate production methods, cycle time, equipment performance, and materials/components in support of production targets. The work model for the role is : #LI-OnSite 

This role is contributing to the Electrification Business in Apodaca, Nuevo Leon. 

 You will be mainly accountable for: 

 • Identifying and recommending improvement opportunities and implements improvement projects, ensuring adherence to timeframe, quality, and cost requirements.
• Approving the design for processes developed internally or externally and performing final tests with respect to the project.
• Providing support to Production during the internal/external process/equipment start-up, defining action plans and training relevant maintenance and production resources.
• Evaluating new process technologies to improve productivity, quality, and cost reduction, defining and leading testing activities, approval criteria, and external provider choices.

 Qualifications for the role: 

 • Bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical, mechatronics, industrial, or a related engineering field. 
• 3+ years of experience in similar positions as a manufacturing and process engineer with experience in essential manufacturing and assembly processes.
• Experience with AutoCAD 2D  layout management  (SolidWorks 3D preferred). 
• Knowledge of capacity calculations, creating and updating manufacturing routes in SAP and experience managing OPEX and CAPEX savings projects.
• Experience with Lean Manufacturing. (Green Belt certification preferred). 
• Advanced English proficiency.

 More about us 

 Building a cleaner, smarter future takes all kinds of minds: the curious, the courageous, and the creative. That's why we welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences.

 Ready to make an impact? 

 Apply today or visit https://www.abb.com to learn more about the impact of our solutions across the globe.

This person will work closely with cross-functional teams to improve safety, quality, delivery, and cost by solving shop-floor challenges, advancing manufacturing capability, and supporting production readiness for new and existing products. The ideal candidate combines strong manufacturing expertise, hands-on problem solving, and the ability to guide others in a fast-paced production environment.

In this role, you will help improve manufacturing capability, support production readiness, solve critical shop-floor challenges, and enable safe, high-quality delivery for the business. This is primarily a individual contributor role with opportunities to provide coaching, mentorship and project management through influence. 

 Job Description 
 Roles and Responsibilities

jobs.title: Lead, Manufacturing Engineer, Integration & Test
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Mechanisms & Integrated Sub-Assemblies Manufacturing team at Relativity Space is currently in the design release and New Product Introduction phase for Terran R, our next generation, fully re-useable rocket. This team handles a broad range of responsibilities, collaborating closely with vehicle design, factory test and production to develop hardware that supports rocket reusability. This includes key assemblies like pneumatic separation and release mechanisms, linear and rotary electromechanical actuators and Integrated propulsion/avionics assemblies. Additionally, the team is responsible for optimizing factory floor layouts and designing and implementing intricate tooling and processes. Unique to Relativity, you will get to work across many teams to iterate and support development of the vehicle program. To be successful in this role, you need to be a self-starter that can thrive in ambiguity, identify problems and quickly resolve them, and provide definition to the previously undefined. You should have a commitment to quality and the discipline required to achieve it. 

 About the Role: 

• Lead and mentor a team of manufacturing engineers building flight-ready mechanisms and integrated sub-assemblies, driving scalable, efficient, and high-quality production processes. 

• Own a major mechanized assembly and/or integrated sub-assembly, contributing directly to build development while guiding team execution from design release through production. 

• Coordinate cross-functional efforts across design, supply chain, and production to execute the build process: covering planning, sourcing strategies, sequencing, mBOM development, tooling, equipment and work order creation. 

• Guide workcenter development with a strategic focus on long-term goals, safety, capital investment, and tooling, aligning operations with scaling and continuous improvement objectives. 

• Provide hands-on technical leadership to resolve manufacturing challenges, lead root cause analysis, and implement sustainable, efficiency-driven solutions. 

• Manage team priorities, offer technical direction, drive execution, and support professional development of team members. 

 About You: 

• 5+ years of relevant work experience and BS degree in aerospace, mechanical, electrical, manufacturing engineering or related technical field. 

• Extensive experience authoring work instructions, mBOMs and technical procedures for interdisciplinary assemblies involving mechanical, electrical, and pneumatic systems. 

• Proven ability to work cross-functionally with design, manufacturing, production, and quality teams to execute and optimize build processes. 

• Strong understanding of mechanisms manufacturing and integrated assembly processes across mechanical, electrical, and pneumatic systems. 

• Experience executing and driving projects in a fast-paced, evolving environment. 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Previous experience leading or mentoring engineering teams. 

• Experience with scaling manufacturing processes from development through rate production. 

• Hands-on experience with RCCA, assembly testing, tooling design and/or fabrication. 

• Experience in capacity analysis, PFMEA, value stream mapping and work center/process development. 

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here. 

 Hiring Range:
 $132,000 — $198,000 USD 

 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 

 If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at accommodations@relativityspace.com . 

 Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission - via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee - will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.
